since the first, and it has risen and the series has not fallen since the twentieth of this month. **THE AGGREGATE OF THE FOUR BODIES OF HOUSEHOLDS HAS NOT MOVED IN TWENTY-ONE DAYS AND THE SENTENCE SAYING SO HAS NOW BEEN WRITTEN ON TWENTY OF TWENTY-TWO MORNINGS, the two it was not written on being the ninth and the tenth of this month, and the man who wrote on the fifteenth of this month that he would stop writing it in about four days has not stopped.** Four people go up the cart road past the ford and off it at about the seventh hour of the morning: the reader of this body, the man of about fifty, the man of about thirty-one of Silling, and **an officer of the Office of the Continuity who is not named in this book and is not named anywhere, and the fen enters the reason, which is that a person an office sends and a person an office has written down are two different objects, and that a name in this book is a thing an office can use, and that the fen does not know what an office would use it for.** The clerk stayed at the node with a book. **The walk is four miles from the top of a valley above this holding down and east to a valve house at the bottom of the water, the line is under the turf the whole way and comes up into two valve boxes and both were open and both were clean, and there are ELEVEN PLACES IN FOUR MILES WHERE THE GROUND OVER THE LINE HAS BEEN OPENED AND MADE GOOD AGAIN, and the eleven are not evenly spaced, and at the ninth of the eleven there is a branch and at the other ten there is ground and not wood.** The office's own line is a different line, four hundred miles off in one direction and a good deal more in the other, its last entry on the book is a flushing on the nineteenth of a month seven months back, and **this holding has never walked it.** The officer is not obstructive, puts the sheet on the valve box for all four to read before he uses it, and says out loud that he is a man behind a list and not a man behind a man, that the schedule is correct and was carried out, that he did not carry it out and there was nobody from that office within nine days of the date on it, and that **he is here because a body of households that corresponds is a body of households that can be found, and you found yourselves by writing to us.** The reader of this body answers one part and not the other, reason first, and enters that the man's own sentence from the eighteenth of this month has come back up the road in a leather case and that a man's own sentence being used against him is a cost and not a defeat. The man of about fifty says one thing at the bottom valve box, reason first, and enters that both boxes were open when they got there and that if a box is opened on a day with a name on it the name will be on the box and not on the four of them. **A SCAR IS A PLACE WHERE LIVING ROOTWOOD HAS BEEN CUT BACK AND HAS HEALED. A BREAK IS A PLACE WHERE IT HAS NOT. A REDUCTION IS A FIGURE THAT IS SMALLER THAN THE FIGURE BEFORE IT ON THE SAME INSTRUMENT IN THE SAME PLACE. Nobody thanked anybody and nothing tender was said on the top of a valley.**

**267 — *What A Scar Is And What It Is Not*** (day 474, a Thursday, the twenty-fourth)
The fourth line of the rota came round and there was nobody at the headland above Marden and **the number of fields that have waited is sixteen, all sixteen of them the fourth line, and the rota stands at forty-five mornings in force, twenty-nine taken and sixteen not.** The third launder measures **six hundred and ten**, and it has fallen, and it is the first fall since the twentieth of this month. They pace the eleven places out with a cord off the man of about fifty's belt: the shortest is about ninety yards, the longest about two hundred and forty, the ninth and the tenth are about sixty yards apart, and nobody can say why the eleven are where they are and the reader of this body does not ask the officer. **THE INSTRUMENT IS A STEEL WIRE ON A LOOP AND A RULE OF ELEVEN INCHES, the wire fourpence the yard and two yards cost eight pence, the rule and the bag eleven years in the keeping of the man of about fifty, and the practice is two readings and no more than two: the girth above the mark and the width across the face, and a figure smaller than the figure before it on the same instrument in the same place is a reduction, while a branch that is whole and smaller than it was is reduced with no figure to say so until there are two readings.** At ten of the eleven places there is no wood and nothing to read; at the ninth the face is smaller than the girth and there is a roll, **and a roll means the wood is closed and no roll and no closing is a break, and a break and a scar are not two words for one thing and cannot be used for one another.** The officer compares his office's figure with the wire and does not put the two in his book, and then says out loud, reason first: **there is no figure anywhere in his office or in any list he has seen for how fast a roll grows, and a face that has healed is a face that has healed and he cannot tell you when, and a scar has no date in it.** The reader of this body says it back in about four people and not in a yard, and enters that **the count of numbers this holding has handed out that it cannot check is two and the figure he has just not written is not going to be the third.** He then **names the standing rule on the wall of the seed house and does not use it** and asks for that to be entered, and the fourth naming is four namings and is not a use. Nobody thanked anybody.

**268 — *Reduced And Not Broken*** (day 475, a Friday, the twenty-fifth)
The first line of the rota came round at the second hour and was worked and the third launder measures **six hundred and thirteen**, and it has risen. The man of about thirty-one of Silling puts the wire on the branch at the ninth place: **the girth above the mark is eleven inches and two sixteenths by the wire against eleven and three sixteenths by the rule, so that the two disagree by exactly one sixteenth and the wire is the figure, the width across the face is eight inches and nine sixteenths, and the difference is two inches and nine sixteenths, and it is entered as a difference and not as a size and is NOT entered as a reduction, because a reduction needs a figure before it on the same instrument in the same place and this was the first time the instrument had been on that wood.** The roll is over the face and the closing is square. The officer reads out the fourth page of the office's own schedule, which gives the season's window on that line as **the sixth of a month to the eleventh of the same month, not extended in any season**, and the last date of work against that line as **the ninth of a month two months back, which is inside the window**, and prints at the foot that the schedule is correct and is carried out and that nobody from that office is required to be within nine days of the date. **IT HOLDS NO FIGURE FOR THE WIDTH OF A SCAR OVER A CUT.** The man of about thirty-one of Silling says the most likely thing anybody has said about that branch in three days, reason first, and is not agreed with: a man opening ground in a line takes the bank with him. The reader of this body refuses it in about nine people, reason first, and gives two reasons: **a man with a spade in a hurry does not leave a roll, and the date is on a page and the cut is in a piece of wood and nothing on that bank has put them on the same page except that sheet, and a date is a thing a nail and a string put on a wall and this holding has not got that nail and that string and is not going to send for them.** And then, reason first, count seventy-seven: **a branch that is reduced is not a branch that is damaged, and he is right about the difference, and he has no figure for the size of the reduction and is not going to invent one, and a man in about four years will be told he does not know and that he knew on the twenty-fifth of this month that he did not know.** The officer then says the thing that makes the next two days: **what answers it is not a schedule but a ledger, the ledger is public and may be copied, it has a column with a heading and a column with nothing at the head of it, and it is ninety-one rows long.** Nobody thanked anybody.

**269 — *Her Own Morning*** (day 476, a Saturday, the twenty-sixth)
The second line came round at the second hour and was worked and the third launder measures **six hundred and twelve**, and it has fallen again. The reader of this body walks the eleven hundred yards to the gate with the man of about thirty-one of Silling and **asks the woman of about thirty-eight of Marden no question, and the count of the times he has asked her one in this holding's book is nil and did not move.** About twenty-five people are at the gate and about eleven of them work that ground. **THE GREEN HAS NOT CHANGED IN ABOUT FOUR DAYS AND NO FIGURE HAS BEEN PUT AGAINST IT AND NONE IS GOING TO BE.** She says it before anybody asks, reason first, count six: **the ground behind that gate comes off before the middle of next month, the carted part goes to her three animals, the rest is left where it grew and is taken by nobody, she is putting no row on that ground this season, she did not sow it, she does not know what it is, and she is not going to build on a thing she did not put there.** The fen enters that the **decision of the eleventh of last month stands and is not reversed by silence and is not going to be reversed by a gate**, that the count of questions available to a room and not taken is ten and is not said in a yard, and that the reader of this body is in about twenty-five people at a gate while the woman who owns the ground tells nine acres of it to be cut off and says nothing, and that the first of those two facts is the only reason the second one was hers to take. The seedwright of a trust, up from the fen road on the Friday, not sent for, says one sentence about the crop and one about the fruit, reason first, count two: **the question is who put it there and nobody in that yard knows, and a crop is a thing a person did and what is on that ground is a thing that happened to a field.** The woman of about thirty-eight of Marden says the second thing, reason first, count seven: **she is not going to eat one of the fruiting bodies and is not going to say one word about whether they are fit to eat, in that yard or any other, and the dead wood is inside the eleven acres and she is not the one who speaks for the eleven acres.** The reader of this body says out loud in about twenty-five people, reason first, count seventy-eight: **nobody in this holding knows whether that fruit is fit to eat**, and enters that **a claim about the ground and a statement about this holding are two kinds of thing, and the count of four did not move and this is not a fifth.** The cost of her decision is named by her in eleven words and by nobody else: **I am the one in this yard who has had nothing green in her hand in about four days.** What she decided is entered as a decision and not as a figure, and it is the only decision in this holding's book in four years entered as a decision. Nobody thanked anybody.

**270 — *The Ledger, Which Is Incomplete*** (day 477, a Sunday, the twenty-seventh)
The third line came round at the second hour and was worked and the third launder measures **six hundred and fifteen**, and it has risen. The third, the seventh and the eleventh of the eleven places are measured before the ledger is opened, at about the second, the fifth and the sixth hours of the afternoon, and all three are whole and smaller than they were and none of the three is broken, and the roll is over each face and each face is square. **THE FOURTH OF THE FOUR, THE BRANCH AT THE NINTH PLACE, WAS MEASURED ON THE TWENTY-FIFTH, SO THAT ALL FOUR CLAIMED IN THE CHAPTER ARE NOW MEASURED ON THE PAGE AND NONE IS CARRIED.** **THE FOUR OF THE ELEVEN ON THIS LINE ARE THE THIRD, THE SEVENTH, THE NINTH AND THE ELEVENTH, and seven of the eleven are not on this line and this holding cannot get to them, and the standing it has is the standing of a body of households that corresponds, which is a body that can be found and is not a body that can be sent.** The officer left the ledger at the node on the Saturday evening and the reader of this body did not open it until the second hour of the afternoon of the Sunday, and gives the reason. **IT IS READ OUT WHOLE IN ABOUT ELEVEN PEOPLE IN THE ORDINARY HAND: NINETY-ONE ROWS, FIVE COLUMNS WITH HEADS, A SIXTH WITH NOTHING AT THE HEAD OF IT, ONE PRINTED LINE ABOVE THE SIXTH SAYING IT IS NOT MAINTAINED AT ROW LEVEL, AND AT THE FOOT THAT THE FIVE HEADED COLUMNS ARE COMPLETE ON ALL NINETY-ONE ROWS AND THE SIXTH IS BLANK ON ELEVEN OF THEM, THE ELEVEN BEING LISTED IN A DISTRICT RETURN WHICH IS NOT ENCLOSED.** The reader of this body says it once in about eleven people, reason first, count seventy-nine: **a ledger that says what it does not have is worth more than one that does not say, and the proof that one thing is the same as four other things is a record and not an instrument, because an instrument only ever tells you about the thing you put it on, and the record is incomplete and credible and those are four separate things and only one of them is a reason to go and look at the other seven.** The man of about fifty copies it and keeps the ruled lines under **the one that has no head**, reason first, count twenty-two, and the speech now says one unheaded column against five headed, which is what the sheet twenty lines above it prints, and **the count of times a person who keeps a book in this holding has said a thing in a yard the engineer of record had not thought of is six and it is seven.** The fen's own hand: **A LEDGER THAT IS INCOMPLETE AND SAYS SO IS A DOCUMENT AND NOT A WINNING.** Nobody thanked anybody.

**271 — *The Twenty-First Return*** (day 478, a Monday, the twenty-eighth) — **THE TWENTY-FIRST NINTH-DAY RETURN**
The fourth line came round and there was nobody at the headland above Marden and **the number of fields that have waited is seventeen, and the rota stands at forty-six mornings in force, twenty-nine taken and seventeen not.** The third launder measures **six hundred and fourteen**. The barrow comes up the four miles in about an hour and three-quarters behind the man of about thirty-one of Silling, who does not push it once. **THE TWENTY-FIRST NINTH-DAY RETURN WAS MADE AND WEIGHED AT ONE HUNDRED AND SEVENTY-THREE HUNDREDWEIGHT AND IT IS THE ELEVENTH NAME-PAIR IN ELEVEN YEARS, a name into BY and a name into WITNESSED BY, read one at a time by each of the four bodies of households.** It is reconciled twice on the page: **one hundred and sixty-two plus eleven, and also one hundred and fifty-one plus twenty-two.** The chain behind it is entered whole and in order: **one hundred and forty, then eighty-seven, made two days late on the twenty-fourth of a month two months back and the smallest of the eleven, then ninety-two, ninety, eighty-nine and ninety-one**; the interval from the eighty-seven to the one hundred and forty was **nine days and not seven, and it would have been seven if the day had been moved with the figure, and the man of about fifty did not move it.** **THE FOUR FIGURES OF ONE HUNDRED AND FORTY, FIFTY-ONE, SIXTY-TWO AND SEVENTY-THREE ARE EACH ELEVEN ABOVE THE ONE BEFORE IT, WHICH IS THREE INTERVALS AND NOT FOUR, AND THE FEN HAS ENTERED THE THREE.** The next figure if the pattern holds is one hundred and eighty-four, and the reader of this body wrote that in his own book and **did not say it out loud in the yard, because a man who says a number before it is on a page has put it on a page.** Harlan Vetch, of about fifty-eight, leaves the second rule blank for the **fifth** time, and **the count of the returns at which he has not written in it is five, the blanks being the seventeenth, the eighteenth, the nineteenth, the twentieth and this one, and the first of the five is the seventeenth, and this holding does not know what was in that rule on the seventeenth and is not going to ask.** He then says one thing in about nineteen people, reason first, count six: **his three questions are still his and he is not going to ask them again until somebody writes an answer to one of them down in a book, and until there is an answer under them they are not a demand, they are three questions.** The reader of this body, five days off on the Saturday, is at this holding and not at the node, reads the three questions out of the book in about four people, **does not answer them**, and enters the reason, which is that the answer is still four seconds long and he has had nine days of it, and that he is not going to do it on a morning the number went up because a man who answers a question on a morning the number went up is answering a different question. He reads the day-minus rules out loud before either number and says one thing in about four people about the eleventh name-pair in eleven years, reason first, count eighty.

**272 — *What A Page Of A Page Is*** (day 479, a Tuesday, the twenty-ninth)
The first line came round at the second hour and was worked and the third launder measures **six hundred and seventeen**, and the four days of walking the line are over. **THE CRATE THE BOOK CAME DOWN IN IS IN THE CART SHED AND IT IS EMPTY AND IT HAS BEEN EMPTY SINCE THE TWENTY-SECOND OF A MONTH TWO MONTHS BACK: the receipt tied to the handle in a loop of string is one shilling and fourpence and the man of the road wrote nothing under the lid, the oilcloth is in it and folded back, there is no lock and there is a hasp and the hasp is not fastened, and the key is in it, and the key was on a ring for eleven years and came off the ring and went into a crate. THE BOOK IS NOT.** The man of about fifty says it out loud, reason first, count twenty-three: **nobody wrote to anybody to ask for the book to come down, and a crate coming back empty is a crate coming back empty and not a man forgetting, and he has had four days with a key in a shed and has not said one word about it until now, and the reason he is saying it is that the reader of this body is about to write four lines and go up the same road, and if he goes up it without writing in his own book that the book is not here, then in about four years there will be two records of this and one of them will be wrong.** **The count of times a person who keeps a book in this holding has said a thing in a yard the engineer of record had not thought of is seven and it is eight.** Four lines and a fifth go up the four-day road at about the seventh hour of the evening, at this holding's cost, and they ask for the book, name no person, buy no crate because there is a crate, and **the fifth line is that he is not asking for any page of it to be written out for him, because the moment a person asks for a missing page they have asked a person to remember something for them, and a thing remembered for a person is not a page.** The cost is entered whole and read out: **five shillings and no crate, and the box, which held nine pounds and thirteen shillings and eight pence on the twentieth of this month, holds nine pounds and eight shillings.** The reader of this body then says what a page of a page is, in about nine people, reason first, count eighty-one: **the book is a page somebody wrote down out of an instrument, the thing the office sent is a page somebody wrote down out of a kind of thing, a record in a room with a counter is a record and not the thing, and a page of a page is the only one of the three that anybody can copy, and the copy is the one that is wrong.** And: **THE PANEL IS NOT PRINTED, the book is four hundred miles and four days off and will not be in that shed until about the seventh hour of the evening of the seventh of this month if the road allows, and the cheapest instrument in this holding is the bead and he is not going to use it, because a bead reads what a node has recently had done to it and a branch is not a page.** Nobody thanked anybody.

**273 — *The Standing For The Month*** (day 480, a Wednesday, the thirtieth)
The second line came round at the second hour and was worked and the third launder measures **six hundred and sixteen**, and the series is **thirty figures on thirty mornings and not one of the thirty the same as any of the other twenty-nine.** The day-minus rules are read out loud before either number: **the boards at four hundred and fourteen days and the March's tin at four hundred and sixty-one**, which is day minus sixty-six and day minus nineteen. **THE STANDING FOR THE MONTH OF THE FOURTH MONTH IS READ OUT AT ABOUT THE ELEVENTH HOUR OF THE MORNING AT NINE HUNDRED YARDS OFF IN ABOUT TWENTY-FIVE PEOPLE, BY THE PERSON WHO KEEPS THE SEED HOUSE AND READ BACK BY THE CLERK, and it stands in the open and takes about eleven minutes, and the reader of this body is in that yard because he wrote it in his own book on the eleventh of this month in about nineteen people in a yard at Errow Reach and the sentence is nineteen days old and he has not taken it back.** The standing is entered whole: the compost line paid and not a measurement; the leak at three-quarters of an inch with three reasons and no fourth; the beat not logged and its column not opened; **the use log at fifteen lines, and a ledger, a road, a wire and a key in a shed are not contacts and a person is**; five figures of the well at Cauldron Reach all five feet and four feet of shortfall not decomposed and no entry anywhere for that well coming back; **THE SEVENTH COLUMN IS READ AND IS FORTY-FIVE;** five bodies at the node and the number not given in a yard; nineteen fetchings of the man of about seventy and the first of this month not one of them; fifty-three and fifty-three; **the count of entries carrying a day and no figure standing at three and not moving even though a figure came in on the twentieth.** **The man of the north row with the cough is in that yard and is not asked to be in it and says nothing, and the count of yards he has stood in since the first of a month four months back is twenty-five and the count of the times he has said nothing at all in a yard is eight.** The man of about fifty says one thing about the door, reason first, count twenty-four: **he has wanted somebody to write a heading on one of the six blanks every year for four years and has not asked, because a heading is a promise that somebody is going to keep putting a figure in it and he would have to be that somebody and he has not got a second thing to put in it.** The count of things a person who keeps a book in this holding has said in a yard the engineer of record had not thought of is **eight and it is nine.** The reader of this body says the thing he came for, reason first, count eighty-two, and does not say the second sentence of the eleventh because it would be a thing about a woman's ground said in a yard about a well house door. The series goes into his own hand whole. Nobody thanked anybody.

**274 — *The First Of The Fifth Month*** (day 481, a Thursday) — **THE MONTH TURNS**
**THE MONTH TURNED IN THE NIGHT.** The third line came round at the second hour and was worked and the third launder measures **six hundred and nineteen**, the thirty-first figure in a series that has not repeated one figure since the first. **FROM THIS MORNING IN THIS BOOK *THE FIRST* MEANS THE FIRST OF THIS MONTH AND *THE FIRST OF LAST MONTH* MEANS THE FIRST OF THE MONTH THAT ENDED YESTERDAY, AND BOTH ARE TRUE ON THE SAME PAGE FROM TO-DAY FORWARD.** The day-minus rules are read out loud before either number, **the boards at four hundred and fifteen days and the March's tin at four hundred and sixty-two**, which is day minus sixty-six and day minus nineteen. **THE COMPOST LINE FOR THE FIFTH MONTH FALLS ON THIS MORNING AND IS ENTERED WHOLE: THE WORD BEFORE THE FIGURE IS PAID AND HAS BEEN THE SAME WORD THREE MONTHS RUNNING, WHICH IS THE FIRST TIME THAT WORD HAS REPEATED THREE TIMES, THE FIGURE IS ONE HUNDRED POUNDS, THE RUN GOES FROM FIFTEEN NOT DISCHARGED IN FIFTEEN TO SIXTEEN NOT DISCHARGED IN SIXTEEN, AND THE LINE IS NOT A MEASUREMENT OF THE GROUND.** The standing for the first is read out at nine hundred yards off in about twenty-five people and read back by the clerk in about nine minutes, and the only two lines that differ from the standing of the thirtieth of last month are the two: **THE SEVENTH COLUMN IS READ TO-DAY AND IS FORTY-SIX, the door is read on the first and the thirtieth and the column has moved twice in four days for the first time in four years, and the reason it has moved twice in four days is the same reason it moves at all, which is that somebody read a door; and A MAN OF ABOUT SEVENTY IS FETCHED ON THE FIRST OF A MONTH AND WAS NOT FETCHED, and the count is nineteen and did not move, and the standing does not enter why.** The reader of this body does not ask anybody why. Then he stands in front of that door in about five people, and the door is entered whole: **eight feet of board, six columns with no heads for four years, a seventh with a head and forty-six under it, and none of the seven is about the well on the shelf, and the door is nine hundred yards from the seed house and the two are not the same thing.** The man of about fifty says one thing, reason first, count twenty-five, and the premise is now the canon's premise and not a contradiction of it: **the six have had nothing at the head of any of them for four years and nothing against any of them for four years, and he has worked out which one of the six he would write in first, and he has known which one for about two years and has not said it out loud to anybody, and he will tell a room and not a yard.** THE WITHHELD-KNOWLEDGE BEAT IS UNCHANGED AND IT NO LONGER REQUIRES FIGURES IN COLUMNS THAT HAVE NEVER HELD ONE. The reader of this body says one thing, reason first, count eighty-three: **those eleven lines are the only thing this holding says out loud every month that anybody outside it ever hears, and for four years this holding has read them out twice a month and improved nothing and asked nothing, and that is the whole of what a body with no charter has been able to do in a month for four years, and it is not nothing.** Nobody thanked anybody.

**275 — *Held For Five*** (days 482 and 483, a Friday and a Saturday) — **THE BATCH CLIMAX. ZERO `Entered ...` BLOCKS.**
The fourth line of the rota came round on the second of this month at the second hour and there was nobody at the headland above Marden and **the number of fields that have waited is eighteen, all eighteen of them the fourth line, and the rota stands at forty-seven mornings in force, twenty-nine taken and eighteen not, and twenty-nine and eighteen are forty-seven.** The third launder measures **six hundred and eighteen** on the second and **six hundred and twenty** on the third, and the eleven figures of the eleven days since the twenty-third of last month have fallen five times and risen six times, and the series is **thirty-three figures on thirty-three mornings and not one of the thirty-three the same as any of the other thirty-two.** **A PATTERN IS HELD FOR FIVE ACROSS TWO BRANCHES ABOUT THREE HUNDRED YARDS APART ON THE SHOULDER ABOVE THE LOCAL LEAD LINE, IN ABOUT THREE PEOPLE, THE MAN OF ABOUT FIFTY AND THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-ONE OF SILLING HAVING BEEN TOLD AT ABOUT THE SECOND HOUR WHAT WAS GOING TO BE DONE AND HOW LONG AND NEITHER HAVING ASKED WHAT FOR. IT IS A HOLD AND NOT A DRAW AND HE TAKES NOTHING OUT OF IT.** The man of about fifty calls a word at about four minutes and eleven seconds and the reader of this body goes on for about eleven seconds after the word, and the fen enters that **the man of about fifty is not a licensed man, that the four lines on the wall of that seed house say the stop is to be called by a licensed man, that a rule with four lines about a draw does not reach a hold, and that a man working to the fourth of four lines when the four lines do not apply is a man who has made a habit and not a practice.** The reader of this body sat down, not fell, and sat about nine minutes before he could stand without putting a hand on something, and **his hand from the wrist down had a use all the afternoon, which it did not have on the twenty-first of a month two months back.** **THE COST: THE SECOND WORD OF THE FIFTH LINE OF THE COVENANT OF SIX LINES IS NOT THERE. IT WAS THERE AT THE FOURTH HOUR OF THE AFTERNOON ON THE SECOND OF THIS MONTH AND IT WAS NOT THERE AT THE FIFTH HOUR AND IT DID NOT COME BACK IN NINE MINUTES THIS TIME, AND NOBODY BUT HIM HAS EVER HAD IT AND HE DID NOT SAY.** He does not go and read the covenant, which is on the middle table in the seed house and which anybody may walk up and read, and enters the reason: **a man who goes and reads a thing he has lost the first time it happens has established that the second time he will read it, and a man who reads it the second time stops noticing the third time.** **The counts are entered in his own hand and none of them moved: two can hold a pattern for four, one can hold for five and it is him, two have a rootmark — one of them a man of about sixty-eight with three inches on the right forearm that do not branch, **and that man is not NAMED in this holding's book, and nothing said about that arm on the second of this month is a third account of it** — one can hold for four and walk out of the ground afterwards, and a hold for five is not a new column.** **AND, IN THE SAME BLOCK AND IN HIS OWN HAND, THE CARD'S LOCKS, WHICH WERE NOT ON THE PAGE WHEN THIS ENTRY WAS FIRST WRITTEN AND ARE NOW: THE MARK ON THIS ARM IS FOUR INCHES AND BRANCHES TWICE AND IS NOT A SECOND MARK AND IS NOT LONGER, THE BURN IS NOT A MARK, THE MARK BEING HOT IS NOT A MARK, AND THE FOUR ACCOUNTS OF THIS ARM ARE FOUR AND NOTHING SAID ABOUT IT TO-DAY IS A FIFTH. THE HEADACHE IS NOT THE MARK IS SEPARATE AND EARLIER IN THE CHAPTER, AT THE COST, AND IS NOT REPEATED HERE.** What the hold gave is entered whole and is not a panel and has no unit: **that two branches three hundred yards apart hold the same shape and that the shape is the shape the eleven blank rows in a copy of a public ledger are in, and that a man's own body saying so is not a record and is worth nothing in front of anybody, and the two agree, and the agreeing is not a proof and he is not going to call it one, and it is not a cause and it is not a name and it is not a date.** Nobody thanked anybody and nothing tender was said. **The last line is not an answer, and none of the four closing items is a name: the four lines went up the four-day road on the twenty-ninth of last month and the road puts them on that shelf at about the seventh hour of the evening of the third of this month, **which is a figure off a road and not off a word, and nobody has said so to him**; and a crate will be in the cart shed on the seventh of this month if the road allows; and neither of those is an answer to anything, and he is not going to write down which of the two things he has got it is.**

## VOLUME 06, BATCH 0004 — Chapters 276-285, days 484-494, Movement 4, *The Two Reasons To Stop* (drafted)

**276 — *The Second Time Somebody Else Decides*** (day 484, a Sunday, the fourth of the fifth month) — **THE SECOND ATTEMPT AT THE CHANNEL DECISION, IN A ROOM**
The second line of the rota came round at the second hour and was worked and the third launder measures **six hundred and twenty-one**, the **thirty-fourth** figure in a series that has not repeated one figure since the first, and it has risen; the aggregate has not moved in thirty-two days and the sentence saying so was written on thirty-one of thirty-three mornings. At about the fourth hour of the afternoon **nine people go into the seed house and the door is shut**: the woman of about thirty-eight of Marden, the man of about thirty-one of Silling, two people this holding cannot place, the man of about fifty, the person who keeps the seed house, the woman who does the sums, the clerk, and the reader of this body. **THE REASON HE IS IN THE ROOM IS READ OUT AT THE SEVENTH HOUR OF THE MORNING, IN ABOUT FOUR PEOPLE, BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE IS SAID IN IT: four bodies of households cannot measure eleven hundred yards and there is one man in this holding who can walk them, and he is in the room as the man who can walk it and not as the engineer of record.** The room does not reopen the sentence of the eleventh of last month and is not entitled to; it asks the four bodies, one at a time, what sentence each of them carried out of that yard, and writes four answers in four hands. **Three of the four are the same eleven words in three hands: *the cut stays open and nothing goes in it this season*. The fourth is the same eleven words with one line under them, and the line is a footing and not a disagreement.** The man of about fifty says his column for that yard has the day, the hour, the number of people and the minutes in it and no words at all, and that it is worth nothing to anybody who was not there. The reader of this body gives eleven hundred yards, a fall of about a foot, two feet of gap, a wire and a rule and eight pence, and about ninety yards along the edge of ground nobody has spoken for, and says he has no figure for how fast a roll grows and nothing whatever about the middle. **THE ROOM DECIDED NOTHING.**

**277 — *What A Room Is For*** (day 485, a Monday, the fifth)
The third line of the rota came round at the second hour and was worked and the third launder measures **six hundred and twenty-two**, the **thirty-fifth** figure, and it has risen twice since the third of this month and has not fallen in those two days at all. At about the fourth hour of the afternoon the same nine people are in the seed house with the door shut and the four answers are read out whole. **NINETEEN PEOPLE WALKED OUT OF A YARD AT ERROW REACH ON THE ELEVENTH OF LAST MONTH CARRYING A SENTENCE, FOUR OF THE NINETEEN WERE THE FOUR BODIES OF HOUSEHOLDS, AND THE OTHER FIFTEEN HAVE NEVER BEEN ASKED WHAT THEY CARRIED OUT OF IT.** The four sheets go on the middle table on top of the covenant of six lines, and the reader of this body does not read the covenant, for the second time, and enters the reason. **THE READER OF THIS BODY SAYS WHAT A ROOM IS: a room in a holding with no charter is a room in a seed house, and the difference between a room and a yard is not how many people are in it, it is whether the people in it have to carry it out of the door or can leave it on the table, and a yard is where a thing gets said that wants company and a room is where a thing gets decided that does not want to be repeated.** The man of about thirty-one of Silling says that agreeing is cheap and writing it down is not. The man of about fifty says that the count he keeps is a count of the yard and not a count of the holding, **and the count of times a person who keeps a book has said a thing in a yard the engineer of record had not thought of is ten and did not move, because this was a room.**

**278 — *The Fourth Line Again*** (day 486, a Tuesday, the sixth)
The fourth line of the rota came round at the second hour and there was nobody at the headland above Marden and **the number of fields that have waited is nineteen, all nineteen of them the fourth line, and the rota stands at forty-eight mornings in force, twenty-nine taken and nineteen not.** The third launder measures **six hundred and twenty-four**, the **thirty-sixth** figure, and it has risen three times since the third of this month and has not fallen in those three days at all. The day-minus rules are read out loud before either number: **the boards at four hundred and twenty days and the March's tin at four hundred and sixty-seven, forty-seven days apart, the drawer not opened.** The rota is read out in a yard at the node in about eleven people, because a rota is a document and a document in this holding is read in the open. **The man of the north row with the cough is in that yard, was not asked to be in it and said nothing; the count of yards he has stood in since the first of a month four months back is twenty-six and the count of the times he has said nothing at all is nine, and the two counts have not been added together.** The man of about fifty says a line that is worked nineteen mornings out of forty-eight is a work line and a line that is empty nineteen mornings out of forty-eight is a place in a table with a name at the head of it, **and the count of times a person who keeps a book in this holding has said a thing in a yard the engineer of record had not thought of is ten and it is eleven.** The man of about thirty-one of Silling says that nineteen is not nineteen fields and that if anybody reads nineteen off that table and thinks nineteen fields are owed, a piece of arithmetic has turned into a debt. The reader of this body stands twenty minutes on the headland, about four hundred yards back from where the ditch begins, and does not walk it.

**279 — *The Twenty-Second Return, And The Crate*** (day 487, a Wednesday, the seventh) — **THE TWENTY-SECOND NINTH-DAY RETURN AND THE CRATE**
The first line of the rota came round at the second hour and was worked and the third launder measures **six hundred and twenty-three**, the **thirty-seventh** figure, and it has fallen once since the third of this month and risen three times, and the fall is the first one since the second of this month. **THE TWENTY-SECOND NINTH-DAY RETURN WAS MADE AND WEIGHED AT ONE HUNDRED AND EIGHTY-FOUR HUNDREDWEIGHT, THE TWELFTH NAME-PAIR IN ELEVEN YEARS, RECONCILED TWICE, BEING ONE HUNDRED AND SEVENTY-THREE PLUS ELEVEN AND ALSO ONE HUNDRED AND SIXTY-TWO PLUS TWENTY-TWO. THE MAN OF ABOUT FIFTY WROTE THAT FIGURE IN HIS OWN BOOK AT ABOUT THE SEVENTH HOUR OF THE EVENING OF THE TWENTY-EIGHTH OF LAST MONTH AND DID NOT SAY IT OUT LOUD, AND THIS HOLDING IS USING THAT DERIVATION AND IS NOT REFUSING IT, AND THE COUNT OF THE TIMES THE SAME FIGURE HAS BEEN ENTERED BY TWO HANDS AND CALLED A CHECK IS FIVE AND IT IS NOT A CHECK.** The four figures of one hundred and forty, one hundred and fifty-one, one hundred and sixty-two and one hundred and seventy-three are each eleven above the one before it, which is **three** intervals. **HARLAN VETCH LEFT THE SECOND RULE BLANK FOR THE SIXTH TIME AND THE COUNT OF THAT IS SIX AND THE BLANKS ARE THE SEVENTEENTH, THE EIGHTEENTH, THE NINETEENTH, THE TWENTIETH, THE TWENTY-FIRST AND THIS ONE, AND HE SAID THAT HIS THREE QUESTIONS ARE STILL HIS AND THAT HE IS NOT GOING TO TURN THEM INTO A COMPLAINT BECAUSE IT IS CONVENIENT IN A ROOM, AND HE WAS NOT THANKED.** At about the seventh hour of the evening **a crate comes down the four-day road into the cart shed at the node**, and the whole arithmetic is on the page, and **nothing was opened in a yard**, because a crate that has come down a four-day road is opened in daylight by the people it was written to.

**280 — *A Fragment, Or A Whole Thing*** (day 488, a Thursday, the eighth)
The second line of the rota came round at the second hour and was worked and the third launder measures **six hundred and twenty-five**, the **thirty-eighth** figure, and it has fallen once and risen four times since the third of this month. At about the eighth hour of the morning the crate is opened in about nine people in the cart shed. **THE THING IN THE OILCLOTH IS A FRAGMENT AND NOT A WHOLE THING: A FRONT BOARD OF ABOUT THE SIZE OF A FIVE-POUNDS LOAF WITH A BEAD FIXED IN IT, AND ELEVEN PAGES. THE BEAD IS LIVING ROOTWOOD AND IT IS ALIVE AND IT IS THE SIZE OF A PEA AND IT HAS A CUT END AND NO COPPER ON IT AT ALL, AND IT IS NOT THE WITNESS BEAD AND IT WAS NOT PUT AGAINST ANYBODY'S ARM. MOST OF THE SURVEY PAGES ARE GONE AND NOBODY IN THIS HOLDING HAS EVER KNOWN WHERE THEY WENT AND HE ASKED FOR NONE OF THEM. THE PANEL IS NOT PRINTED AND THE COUNT OF ITS USES IS ONE AND IT IS A COUNT OF ITS OWN.** **THE FRONT BOARD CARRIES NINE LINES, EACH WITH A DATE, A PLACE AND ONE WORD, AND THERE IS NOTHING AT THE HEAD OF THE COLUMN. THE FIRST EIGHT PLACES ARE PLACES THIS HOLDING CANNOT GO TO. THE NINTH IS ABOUT NINE MILES FROM THE STONE HEAD, IS DATED THE TWELFTH OF LAST MONTH, AND SAYS NO CUT.** The man of about thirty-one of Silling refuses to call it a second witness, because a word and a figure are one person saying two things, and saves the reader of this body from writing a figure he has not measured, and the count of numbers this holding has handed out that it cannot check is two and did not move. The man of about fifty says he will enter the loss as a line of its own and keep the ruled lines under the pages that are not there, for the same reason he kept them under the sixth column of the office's ledger.

**281 — *The First Refusal*** (day 489, a Friday, the ninth) — **A REFUSAL THAT NAMES A FIGURE**
The third line of the rota came round at the second hour and was worked and the third launder measures **six hundred and twenty-seven**, the **thirty-ninth** figure, and it has fallen once and risen five times since the third of this month. Eleven people are in the seed house with the door shut and the form with four lines on it is on the middle table with three of the lines empty. **THE FIGURE ON THE MIDDLE TABLE SINCE THE FOURTH OF THIS MONTH IS SIX HUNDRED AND TWENTY-ONE HUNDREDWEIGHT, WHICH IS THE FIGURE OFF THE THIRD LAUNDER ON THE FOURTH, AND IT WAS PUT THERE BY THE READER OF THIS BODY AND BY NOBODY ELSE, AND IT WAS STILL THERE ON THE NINTH.** The four sheets and the form are two different questions and the room has been treating them as one for five days. The woman of about thirty-eight of Marden says the eleven words are about a gap and the four lines are about a length and refuses to put a figure on any of them. **A BODY OF HOUSEHOLDS REFUSES AND THE REFUSAL NAMES A FIGURE: the man of about thirty-one of Silling, for Silling, refuses six hundred and twenty-one hundredweight, which is five days old and off a dial four miles off at a node this holding does not steward, and says he is not refusing the figure and is refusing to build four lines on it, and that no person in that room had ever had it read to them and no name of his is against it anywhere. HE WAS NOT THANKED.** He gives his body's figure in its place: **one hundred and eighty-four hundredweight**, off a steelyard, with his own name and a second name against it in two columns, read out to that body of households twelve times in eleven years. The reader of this body says out loud, before anybody else does, that **a refusal that names a figure is a refusal about a figure, and the other kind names a person, and a room that has one of each and no word on which is which has made a mess and not a decision.**

**282 — *The Second Refusal*** (day 490, a Saturday, the tenth) — **A REFUSAL THAT NAMES A PERSON**
The fourth line of the rota came round at the second hour and there was nobody at the headland above Marden and **the number of fields that have waited is twenty, all twenty of them the fourth line, and the rota stands at forty-nine mornings in force, twenty-nine taken and twenty not.** The third launder measures **six hundred and twenty-six**, the **fortieth** figure, and it has fallen twice and risen five times since the third of this month, and it has fallen. Eleven people are in the seed house with the door shut and the man of about fifty stands up before anybody has said anything and says, giving the reason first, that **a blank line is a question that was not answered and a blank space is a question that was not asked, and those are two different objects that he has been writing down in the same hand all year.** **A SECOND BODY OF HOUSEHOLDS REFUSES AND THE REFUSAL NAMES A PERSON: the woman of about thirty-eight of Marden, for Marden, names HARLAN VETCH, WHO HOLDS A FIFTH SHARE, HAS HELD IT ELEVEN YEARS AND FORTY-SEVEN DAYS, HAS BEEN WEIGHED TWELVE TIMES IN ELEVEN YEARS, AND HAS NEVER ONCE BEEN IN A LINE, AND WHO IS NOT IN THAT ROOM. She says she has no charge against him and that this holding has not got one either and has not looked for one, and that a yard can be a place where a man who is not in it is talked about and a room is a place where a man who is not in it is not talked about. SHE WAS NOT THANKED.** The man of about thirty-one of Silling declines to name either refusal. She then gives a number in a room and not on the form, **being eleven hundred yards from a stone head to a field gate, walked for about eleven weeks because it is her ditch, not measured, with about ninety yards of it given as part of the eleven hundred and as nothing else**, and nobody in that room said whose the ninety yards is. **A LENGTH IS NOT A CLAIM AND A LENGTH IS NOT A MEASUREMENT. NEITHER REFUSAL WAS A QUARREL.**

**283 — *A Test Against A Public Record*** (day 491, a Sunday, the eleventh)
The first line of the rota came round at the second hour and was worked and the third launder measures **six hundred and twenty-eight**, the **forty-first** figure, and it has fallen twice and risen six times since the third of this month. **Sera Quill is at the seed house at about the fourth hour of the afternoon, having come up the fen road on foot on the evening of the tenth, and nobody had sent for her**, and the count of the times the reader of this body has asked her a question in this holding's book is one and it is still one. She puts her information on the middle table in six lines in her own hand. The copy of the ninety-one-row ledger of the Office of the Continuity is on the table under them. **FIVE OF HER SIX ITEMS WERE PUT AGAINST THAT RECORD AND FIVE HELD**: the fifth headed column carries a word or a figure on all ninety-one rows and **contains nine different words**; the fourth page and the ledger agree on the last date of work against the line, being the ninth of a month two months back, inside a window that is not extended in any season; the sixth column exists, is ruled, and is blank on eleven of ninety-one, and the eleven are listed in a district return which is not enclosed; the sheet of the third of last month carries no figure that could be a fraction, a count of readings or a time; and somebody wrote a judgement of a branch ninety-one times and the judgement is in the record and not in any instruction. **THE READER OF THIS BODY SAYS THAT A PUBLIC RECORD IS A DOCUMENT, THAT A DOCUMENT IS CORRECT AND INCOMPLETE AND PRINTS BOTH, AND THAT WHEN A DOCUMENT PASSES OR FAILS A TEST THE FACT IS ABOUT THE DOCUMENT AND NOT ABOUT WHOEVER WROTE IT, AND THAT NONE OF THE FIVE THAT HELD SAYS ANYTHING ABOUT A CAUSE.** Sera Quill says she has been in five rooms about a list and has not been one of the people in about nineteen years, and that the five of hers that held held for a reason that is not hers. **THE ROOM COMES TO THE SIXTH LINE ON HER SHEET AND THE READER OF THIS BODY DOES NOT READ IT OUT, AND THE REASON IS ON THE PAGE WITH THE HOUR ON IT, AND IT IS THAT ASKING HER A QUESTION IS THE ONE THING HE HAS NOT DONE IN FOUR YEARS.**

**284 — *The One Item That Does Not Hold*** (day 492, a Monday, the twelfth)
The second line of the rota came round at the second hour and was worked and the third launder measures **six hundred and thirty**, the **forty-second** figure, and it has fallen twice and risen seven times since the third of this month. The same nine people are in the seed house with the door shut and **Sera Quill says the sixth item before anybody asks her for it, giving the reason first**: four branches came off a list in her life for being irregular and not one of the four was damaged. **THE RECORD DID NOT HOLD IT AND THE RECORD IS CORRECT: the fifth headed column is condition at last work, which is the condition of a row at the moment somebody last worked it, and no cut is the condition of a stem on a morning when nobody worked it at all, and those are two different moments, and the sixth column is the one that was going to hold the other and it is blank on eleven of ninety-one and the return that lists them is not enclosed.** **A DOCUMENT THAT FAILS A TEST HAS SAID SOMETHING ABOUT ITSELF, AND WHAT THIS ONE SAID IS THAT THE COLUMN IT WOULD NEED HAS NOTHING AT THE HEAD OF IT, AND THE OFFICE PRINTS IN THE MIDDLE OF THE SHEET THAT THE SIXTH COLUMN IS CARRIED IN THE DISTRICT RETURN ONLY. NO OFFICE LIED OR OBSTRUCTED OR DELAYED OR SOFTENED ANYTHING.** The man of about thirty-one of Silling says that at the ninth of the eleven places there is a branch and this holding has no word for it yet, and the word is not damaged, and that whole is a word about a piece of wood and sound is a word about a living thing. She writes the item out in her own hand and leaves it on the middle table. **The reader of this body says he is not going to make anything of her, and enters that four people in that room had a sentence ready and did not say it, and that a person who turns a working finding into a lesson is buying something cheaper than the finding. SHE WAS NOT THANKED.**

**285 — *What The Two Refusals Are For*** (days 493 and 494, a Tuesday and a Wednesday) — **THE BATCH CLIMAX. ZERO `Entered ...` BLOCKS.**
The third line of the rota came round on the thirteenth at the second hour and was worked and the third launder measures **six hundred and twenty-nine**, the **forty-third** figure, and it has fallen three times and risen seven times since the third of this month; the day-minus rules are read out loud before either number and stand at **four hundred and twenty-seven days and four hundred and seventy-four**. At about the fourth hour of the afternoon the fifth room in eight days, and the form is read out whole in two hands on the face of it, neither of them the reader of this body's: **line one, ONE HUNDRED AND EIGHTY-FOUR HUNDREDWEIGHT, in the hand of the man of about thirty-one of Silling, the only figure written on the form**; lines two, three and four blank, two bodies never asked, and the count of blank lines is three and is a count of its own. **THE FIGURE THE FIRST REFUSAL NAMED IS NOT A LINE OF THIS FORM AND IS ON THE BACK OF THE SAME SHEET, NOT CROSSED OUT, WITH THE DAY AND THE HOUR UNDER IT.** And under the four lines two things in two mouths and neither on the sheet, **eleven hundred yards, said in a room and not written down, and a name, also said in that room and not on the sheet either**; and under those one line the man of about fifty wrote himself because the reader of this body said the sentence out loud in that room on the ninth and did not ask him to put it down: **A REFUSAL THAT NAMES A FIGURE IS A REFUSAL ABOUT A FIGURE. A REFUSAL THAT NAMES A PERSON IS A REFUSAL ABOUT A PERSON. A ROOM THAT HAS ONE OF EACH AND NO WORD ON WHICH IS WHICH HAS NOT MADE A DECISION.** The woman of about thirty-eight of Marden says the nine acres come off before the middle of next month and nobody has said a word to her about it in eight days. The reader of this body says **the two refusals were for stopping a decision, and it is not a victory**, and reads out what has not changed: the gap is open, the water is still coming, the nine acres come off, the man who holds a fifth share has not been asked, about ninety yards of eleven hundred has not been walked by anybody, the sixth column is blank on eleven of ninety-one. The fourteenth came round, a Wednesday, the fourth line of the rota came round and there was nobody at the headland and **the number of fields that have waited is twenty-one and the rota stands at fifty mornings in force, twenty-nine taken and twenty-one not, and twenty-nine and twenty-one are fifty**; the third launder measures **six hundred and thirty-one**, the **forty-fourth** figure, and it has fallen three times and risen eight times since the third of this month; the day-minus rules stand at **four hundred and twenty-eight and four hundred and seventy-five**; the rota and the form are read out in a yard at the node in one breath and **the man of the north row with the cough is in that yard and is not asked and says nothing, and the counts are twenty-seven and ten**. The standing count of questions available to a room in this holding and not taken is ten, is not said in a yard, and is put on a page twice in about eleven days. **THE ONLY FIGURES IN THE MOVEMENT'S TURN ARE THE FIGURES THE TWO BODIES GAVE, AND NEITHER OF THEM IS A FIGURE ABOUT THE CHANNEL, AND THE LAST LINE IS NOT AN ANSWER: the line the question is on is entered and not filled, and that line is the third thing that has come out of a room in nine days and it is not one of the two refusals, and nobody did.**

**286 — *A Sheet With A Real Seal On It*** (day 495, a Thursday, the fifteenth)
The first line of the rota came round at the second hour and was worked and the third launder measures **six hundred and thirty-two**, the **forty-fifth** figure, risen, and it has risen nine times and fallen three times since the third of this month. The aggregate has not moved in **forty-three** days and the sentence saying so was written on **forty-two of forty-four** mornings. At about the fourth hour of the afternoon a rider comes up the fen road **on the ordinary post**, is not stopped, and leaves a leather envelope. The wax carries a device the size of a thumbprint, and **the same device is at the head of the copy of the Office of the Continuity's ledger**, so about nine people in the seed house know what it is in about four seconds. The envelope stands unopened for **eleven minutes** and then nine people open it. The sheet is **one page, correct in every particular, no fault found in it**: it names an office four hundred miles off, the **twentieth of this month**, **line 41 of the schedule of the maintenance of the Crown Engine**, says the work is inside the window and that no work on the line is carried out of a window, and says the relay at Low Sike is to be **emptied and sealed**. The man of about fifty says, giving the reason first, that **the word on the sheet which is not a part of the work is *emptied***, and that a building is shut and a thing is emptied and those are two operations. **Soren Rill** comes to the edge of the yard, says the standing form word for the **sixth** time in this holding's book, and then says one more thing, unasked and from the edge: there are **nine sealed places on a list four years old and not his**, Low Sike is the **eighth**, the date on it is the twentieth, and he does not know what is inside it. The reader of this body says that **a relay is a box on the line and the sequence in it opens one valve**, that he has never seen one, and that he does not know what is in it, and that **the next nine days are ours and the proper use of nine days is not to decide anything.** The count of things he has said out loud in a yard and got wrong is four and did not move, and this was a room.

**287 — *The Sixteenth, And The Twenty-Third*** (day 496, a Friday, the sixteenth)
The second line of the rota came round at the second hour and was worked and the third launder measures **six hundred and thirty-four**, the **forty-sixth** figure, risen, and it has risen ten times and fallen three times since the third. The aggregate has not moved in **forty-four** days, written on **forty-three of forty-five**. At about the fourth hour of the morning **the sixteenth ordinary reading of the well on the shelf is taken, four hundred miles and four days off, by the occupier of the first house on that shelf, in her own yard, on her own wall, and this holding enters the day and the hour and NOT the figure, and the count of entries that carry a day and not a figure goes from three to four, which is the only move that count has made in the volume.** Nobody asked for the figure. The wall carries **fourteen marks** and the four feet of shortfall are not decomposed and the tenth reading is not in this holding's book. The day-minus rules are read out loud, **430 and 477**. In the afternoon the **twenty-third ninth-day return** is weighed at the node at **one hundred and ninety-five hundredweight**, the **thirteenth name-pair in eleven years**, reconciled twice, being 184 + 11 and also 173 + 22, and **the page says it is using that derivation and is not refusing it**, and enters that the run of eleven has now held for **five** figures and that **a run that holds for five figures is a run and not a cause**. The reader of this body was at the node and **not at the steelyard when the figure came off**, and that count of two did not move. **Harlan Vetch** leaves the second rule blank for the **seventh** time, the blanks being the seventeenth through the twenty-second and this one, and says in about nineteen people that he has heard a date and did not ask where the two days were going, that his three questions are still his, and that **the count of the times he has offered to be somewhere he is not the engineer of record for is two and is two, and a man who has offered twice and been asked neither time is a man who has learnt the number.** The reader of this body says he does not know whether a sequence in a box can be set against another box, and enters that on the page as a thing he does not know and **not as a seventh of the six written not known against him**, because the six have a unit and that thing has a shape and not a unit.

**288 — *A Condition, In A Room, With Somebody In It Who Is Neither Of Them*** (day 497, a Saturday, the seventeenth)
The third line of the rota came round at the second hour and was worked and the third launder measures **six hundred and thirty-three**, the **forty-seventh** figure, **fallen**, and it is the first fall since the tenth, and it has fallen four times and risen ten times since the third. The aggregate has not moved in **forty-five** days, written on **forty-four of forty-six**. About eleven people are in the seed house with the door shut and **three documents are on the middle table in the order they arrived in and nobody rearranges them**: the sheet with the real seal, the copy of the ledger, and the form with four lines. **Tova Reed defines the word *anchor* before anybody uses it again**, giving the reason first, as **the person who decides when somebody else stops**, says she is not going to be that and that she has said no to it once in her life, and then states **one condition in front of the man of about fifty, who is told that a condition exists and is not told what it is**: *if either of them stops, the other one takes the other one out. Not the seed. The other one. And she is not the person who decides that at the time, because the person who has been in the ground cannot be asked.* **THE STOP WORD IS STILL ONLY HERS AND HE DID NOT ASK FOR IT AND DID NOT KNOW IT, AND IT HAS NOW BEEN SAID TWICE IN THE WHOLE OF THIS HOLDING'S BOOK.** The man of about fifty writes *a condition was stated* and the hour, and **four ruled lines under them, and nothing under those.** The reader of this body then **reads the standing rule out in full, four lines, every one of them about a draw, and says he is not going to use it**, giving the reason first: a rule read out in a room the night before a thing happens is a rule somebody expects to be called, and there is no fifth line and there never has been one, and **the count of times that rule has been named is now six and the count of times it has been used is not at all.** The man of about fifty says he will enter the whole of the sheet, including **the fact that he turned it over in front of eleven people because a page with nothing on the back of it looks like a page somebody did not finish.** Nobody was thanked, and nobody in that room said the word *anchor* again.

**289 — *Low Sike, And A Number Said In A Yard*** (day 498, a Sunday, the eighteenth)
The fourth line of the rota came round at the second hour and **nobody was at the headland above Marden** and the fields waited and the number is **twenty-two**, all of them the fourth line, and the rota stands at **fifty-one mornings in force, twenty-nine taken, twenty-two not**. The third launder measures **six hundred and thirty-five**, the **forty-eighth** figure, risen, and it has risen eleven times and fallen four times since the third. The aggregate has not moved in **forty-six** days, written on **forty-five of forty-seven**. The day-minus rules are read out loud, **432 and 479**. The three who walk are the reader of this body, **Tova Reed** and **Soren Rill**. The man of about thirty-one of Silling walks them to the shed and says the **second person in a room is not a sight** and *do not stand where I would have stood*, and says he will say *I told you so* if they come back and tell him, and takes the barrow back and is not asked to stay. They arrive at Low Sike four hours early on purpose. **THE YARD IS GRAVEL, THIRTY YARDS BY TWENTY, AND THE HASP WAS OFF AND THE DOOR WAS OPEN, AND THE READER OF THIS BODY PUT HIS HAND ON THE DOOR AND STOPPED AND ASKED THREE PEOPLE TO COME UP THE TRACK BEFORE HE WENT IN, BECAUSE A DOOR THAT IS OPEN ON A MORNING WHEN A CREW IS DUE IS NOT AN INVITATION, IT IS A DOOR.** The room is twelve feet by nine with a conduit, an iron plate over its mouth, a tray on a stand, and **a cradle with a hollow in it cut for one thing and four inches of water in the hollow and a thing under the water, and a tinned-iron plate about four inches by two bolted on and not screwed, and a hook on the opposite wall with no key on it. Nobody put a hand in the water and nobody was asked to.** Tova Reed says a hollow is not a mould and that four inches of water in it in a building with no roof means a hand with a spanner has unbolted that plate and put it back a great many times and has never once taken the thing out. Soren Rill says from the edge of the yard that **the word *emptied* on that sheet is a future word** and that on the twentieth a crew is coming to take the thing out and seal the building, and that none of that depends on us and all of it depends on the day. **AND AT ABOUT THE FIFTH HOUR OF THE AFTERNOON THE READER OF THIS BODY SAYS OUT LOUD IN THAT YARD THAT THERE IS ONE RELAY ON THAT LINE AND THAT IT IS THE ONE THEY ARE STANDING IN. THE COUNT OF THINGS HE HAS SAID OUT LOUD IN A YARD AND GOT WRONG IS FOUR ON THAT AFTERNOON. NOBODY ARGUED WITH HIM AND NOBODY CORRECTED HIM.**

**290 — *The Timing, And What The Plate Says*** (days 499 and 500, a Monday and a Tuesday) — **THE BATCH AND VOLUME CLIMAX. ZERO `Entered ...` BLOCKS.**
The first line of the rota came round on the nineteenth at the second hour and was worked and the second line came round on the twentieth at the second hour and was worked, and the third launder measures **six hundred and thirty-seven** on the nineteenth, the **forty-ninth** figure, and **six hundred and thirty-six** on the twentieth, the **fiftieth** figure, fallen, so that it has risen twelve times and fallen five times since the third. The aggregate has not moved in **forty-seven** and then **forty-eight** days, written on **forty-six of forty-eight** and **forty-seven of forty-nine**. The woman of about thirty-eight of Marden is not asked and is not there. **Soren Rill says the sentence about when, giving the reason before he says it, and he makes the timing decision and nobody argues with him and he is right about it:** a crew comes up that track at first light, and a plate unbolted at about the second hour of the morning and put back at about the fourth hour has not been seen, and a plate put back at about the seventh hour has been seen by two men from a cart. **He says he does not know what a crew is like, that he has never been in the room, and that he gave the only thing he was asked for before anybody asked him to.** The plate is read out in the dark by the reader of this body and repeated by Soren Rill and the two readings are the same, and the page says twice that there is no panel. The plate is a `>` block in a maker's hand, six lines, no office, no district, no date, no seal: **FOR VALVE 41-C. ONE VALVE. THIS SEQUENCE IS NOT A VOICE AND IT IS NOT A MIND. IT CANNOT COMMAND ANY MACHINE THAT IS RUNNING. IT OPENS THE VALVE IT IS MADE FOR AND NOTHING ELSE. ROOTWOOD. LIVING.** The thing comes up out of four inches of water about the size of a man's fist, dark, heavier than it looks, with a rough scar at one end, and warm, and he puts his thumb against it and does not press. **AT ABOUT THE FOURTH HOUR OF THE MORNING SHE SAYS THE STOP WORD, AND THE COUNT OF TIMES THAT WORD HAS BEEN SAID IN THIS HOLDING'S BOOK IS TWO, AND THE WORD WAS ENTERED BY THE HOUR AND NOT ENTERED, AND HE STOPPED AT IT, AND THE STOP TOOK ABOUT FOUR MINUTES AND ELEVEN SECONDS.** The plate goes back on, the corner goes down over the water, the door goes on the hasp, and they are at the seed house at about the eighth hour. **THE COST, in his own hand: nine hours with no use in the hand from the wrist down, entered as nine hours and not less; twice sitting down, the second time about nine minutes, unable to stand without a hand on something, not putting a hand on anybody, the other two about nine feet off and neither offering and neither asked; the mark four inches branching twice, not a second mark, not longer; the headache not the mark, not being added together; the four accounts of this arm are four and nothing that happened on the nineteenth is a fifth.** In daylight at about the seventh hour a cart comes up the track with two men and a third on the wheel, the hasp is off, the plate is on the cradle, the four inches of water are in it and **nothing is in the hollow**; each man looks at the cradle for about nine seconds, one says the word *empty*, the other goes and gets a board, the board goes over the conduit mouth, nobody speaks to the man on the wheel, the work is done, they go down the track at about the tenth hour **and do not look back at the yard, and the reason is that they had a sheet.** The reader of this body is nine hundred yards off and does not go and stand in that yard. The man of about thirty-one of Silling says they did not find it out, because a man who finds out says something to the man on the wheel and gets in the cart. The reader of this body says the whole of what is on the table and that **it is worth one valve**, and that **there is one valve at the head of eleven hundred yards of channel at Errow Reach and nobody in this fen has ever seen it**, and that about ninety yards of that eleven hundred has never been walked by anybody here and is still nobody's, and that a valve at the head of a channel does not tell anybody whose the middle of it is. The last line is his own and not a form and not a figure, and it says that **a thing that came back wider than it went in is a contact, and that is a fifth kind, and it is not on this list, and the man of about fifty will have something to say about that and the reader of this body is not going to say it before him.**

**291 — *What Is Under A Cloth*** (day 501, a Wednesday, the twenty-first)
The third line of the rota came round at the second hour and was worked and the third launder measures **six hundred and thirty-eight**, the **fifty-first** figure, risen, and it has risen thirteen times and fallen five times since the third. The aggregate has not moved in **forty-nine** days, written on **forty-eight of fifty**. The day-minus rules are read out loud, **435 and 482**. **THE SEED IS ON THE MIDDLE TABLE UNDER A CLOTH WITH A PAIL OF WATER AND A WET CLOTH AGAINST IT**, and the reason for the cloth is entered in his own hand with the hour on it, and **the person who keeps the seed house did it at about the eighth hour of the morning before anybody said anything about it and was not thanked**, and the count of people in this holding who have looked at it is **nil**. The man of about thirty-one of Silling says **forty-one C is a letter** and that there is a forty-one A and B and D and E, and that a key with a number on it is a key and not a proof, and that a word and a figure are one person saying two things, and that he said that in a shed on the eighth and has not stopped saying it. **Tova Reed says it is not a part**: a part has a number a maker gives it and a list of faults, and there is no list and no fault on the plate and the plate says in its own last line that it is living, and she has a shape and not a name and is not going to tell the room what it is. **Soren Rill says he is not going to say they will come for it**, because he does not know that and is not going to say a thing he does not know with his name on it, and that there is a form of words an office uses when a thing has been in a cradle and is not in a cradle, and **it is not a question, it is a return, and nobody has to have noticed anything for a return to go out.** The man of about fifty says **the use log stands at fifteen lines and is going to stand at fifteen**, and gives the reason once and says he is not going to give it again in a season, and the reason is that **a line in that book has a day and an hour and the name of the person who touched a thing, and a thing a man carried out of a building has a day and an hour and the name of the person who carried it, and only one of those is a contact**, and that a man who starts keeping a record of himself has got two books and about four years later neither of them is any good. The reader of this body says **he is not going to use it**, giving the reason first: there is a valve at the head of eleven hundred yards and this is the only key to it that has ever been in this holding, and he could open it tomorrow morning, and the reason is the sentence of the eleventh of last month, **the cut stays open and nothing is to be put in that gap this season**; and opening the valve at the head is not putting something in the gap, **it is putting nine inches of water on nine acres that a woman decided about on the twenty-sixth of last month**, and the count of the questions he has asked her is nil and is nil this afternoon, and he would have to go and stand in her ground before he said one word about a valve that puts water on it. **NOBODY WAS THANKED AND NOTHING TENDER WAS SAID.**

**292 — *The Memorandum*** (day 502, a Thursday, the twenty-second)
The fourth line of the rota came round at the second hour and **nobody was at the headland above Marden** and the fields waited and the number is **twenty-three**, all of them the fourth line, and the rota stands at **fifty-two mornings in force, twenty-nine taken, twenty-three not**. The third launder measures **six hundred and forty**, the **fifty-second** figure, risen, and it has risen fourteen times and fallen five times since the third. The aggregate has not moved in **fifty** days, written on **forty-nine of fifty-one**. A second rider comes up the fen road on the ordinary post and is not stopped, and the envelope is opened in about eleven minutes in about nine people. **THE MEMORANDUM IS ONE PAGE, DATED THE TWENTIETH AT AN OFFICE FOUR HUNDRED MILES OFF, AND SIGNED AT THE FOOT IN INK BY CHANCELLOR IONA VEY, WHO IS NAMED ON IT AND IS NOT IN THIS HOLDING AND HAS NOT BEEN.** It places **root stewardship on that line in that district under protection from the twentieth**, appoints a person to be present and does not name the person, **says the appointed person is not a steward, and says protection is not stewardship, and the office prints both.** **AND ITS ELEVENTH LINE IS THE ONLY LINE ON IT ABOUT ANYTHING IN THAT ROOM**, and the eleventh line says that no sequence, and no part containing a sequence, and no cradle, is to be removed, broken, opened or set against any valve by any person without a written instrument of the office named at the head of it. **The man of about fifty** enters both documents in the same way and says the sheet of the fifteenth and the memorandum of the twentieth are both correct and both dated the same day, **and that one is about a valley and one is about eleven lines on a page**, and that about nine people read both in about nine minutes and did not see it and that he saw it because he keeps a column for that schedule. **The woman of about thirty-eight of Marden** says, giving the reason first, that she is speaking for nobody but herself, and that her nine acres come off before the middle of next month, and that **a document that arrives after a woman has decided something is not a reason to decide it again.** The reader of this body says the eleventh-line sentence out loud before anybody else does, and says it is not a defeat, and that **three days ago he had a key and a reason not to use it and the reason was a woman nine hundred yards off, and today there is also a document, and the document does not touch the woman and does not name this holding, and the reason is still the woman and not the document.** **THE FORM ON THE MIDDLE TABLE IS STILL FOUR LINES WITH ONE FILLED AND THREE BLANK AND THE LINE THE QUESTION IS ON IS ENTERED AND NOT FILLED, AND THE DOCUMENT DID NOT FILL IT.**

**293 — *Incomplete And Credible*** (day 503, a Friday, the twenty-third)
The first line of the rota came round at the second hour and was worked and the third launder measures **six hundred and thirty-nine**, the **fifty-third** figure, **fallen**, and it has fallen six times and risen fourteen times since the third. The aggregate has not moved in **fifty-one** days, written on **fifty of fifty-two**. About nine people are in the seed house with the door shut with the copy of the ledger and the memorandum of protection on the table, and **Sabra Ollerton, of about fifty-two, inspector of the Rootwright Assembly for four districts, has come up the fen road at her own cost, was not sent for, was not asked to be fed, and says first that she is not on the roll for the district, and that the count of the times anybody in this holding has asked her to corroborate a figure is nil.** The man of about fifty puts the wrong number up first: **there are five rows on that line in his copy, being forty-one A, forty-one B, forty-one C, forty-one D and forty-one E, and the reader of this body said one of them out loud in a yard on the eighteenth, and the correction takes up four lines and is made in a room and not in a yard.** **THE COUNT OF THINGS THE READER OF THIS BODY HAS SAID OUT LOAD IN A YARD AND GOT WRONG WENT OFF FOUR ON TO FIVE, AND IT WAS FOUND BY ANOTHER MAN IN A ROOM FIVE DAYS AFTER IT WAS SAID, AND HE SAID NOTHING WHEN IT WAS READ OUT AND DID NOT PUT THE NUMBER BACK ON THE PAGE.** The reader of this body then says that **the proof this holding has is incomplete and is also credible**, and that the incompleteness is a plate with six lines and no date, a ledger with eleven rows blank in a column with nothing at the head of it, a district return that is not enclosed, and a memorandum that says the appointed person is not a steward, and that the credibility is that two documents from one office in one hand agree with each other about a date and a window, and that **a public record that is both correct and incomplete is the only kind there is**, and that neither of the two can be lent to the other. **Sera Quill, who has been in this holding thirteen days, names the maintained pattern, calls it False Season, defines it in the plain words an instruction would use as a pattern that is maintained and not weather, and says she is not telling them one single thing about how it is done and that if anybody asks her that they have stopped listening to a woman and started at a machine.** Nobody asked. Sabra Ollerton says **the memorandum is not a reward and it is not a punishment**, that it is the ordinary answer to the ordinary question of what happens to a place where something has gone out of a cradle without anybody's leave, and that **a person standing on a line is a good deal safer for the person whose ground it is than eleven people with a wire and a length of ditch**, and that she has no corroboration in her today and is not going to manufacture one out of a career. Nobody was thanked.

**294 — *What Is Left Standing*** (days 504 and 505, a Saturday and a Sunday) — **THE LAST CHAPTER OF VOLUME 06.**
The second line of the rota came round on the twenty-fourth at the second hour and was worked and the third line came round on the twenty-fifth at the second hour and was worked, and the third launder measures **six hundred and forty-one** on the twenty-fourth, the **fifty-fourth** figure, and **six hundred and forty-two** on the twenty-fifth, the **fifty-fifth** figure, so that it has risen sixteen times and fallen six times since the third. The aggregate has not moved in **fifty-two** and then **fifty-three** days. The day-minus rules are read out loud, **438 and 485**, and the reader of this body enters that **the count of mornings he has read them out loud in this month is four and is a count of his own.** About nine people are in the seed house with the door shut with **four objects in a stack on one table**: the seed under a cloth, the memorandum, the form, and the copy of the ledger on the bench, and nobody rearranges the order and nobody looked at the cloth. **The man of about fifty says the word *uneven* out loud, giving the reason first, and will not add to it after today:** eleven hundred yards of water from a stone head to a field gate, about nine acres behind that gate, and the four hundredweight a day of a fifth share that has come out of it for eleven years and has never been in a line; **it was that before the fifteenth of last month and it will be that on the first of next month and on the first of the month after that**, and a person who has spent a month with a sheet in one hand and a cradle in the other is the last person in this fen who gets to be surprised about it. **Nobody offered a second word for it.** The woman of about thirty-eight of Marden gives a date unasked, **the twenty-ninth of next month, or thereabouts**, and says the third time she has said it in a room or a yard is not her reminding anybody of anything, it is her telling them where a man with a valve is going to be standing when the water comes. The reader of this body says what is left standing, and then the standing is read out whole in about nine people: the use log at fifteen, both pattern-holder counts, the two rootmarks, the four accounts of the arm, **five** things said in a yard and got wrong, two numbers this holding cannot check with the first not named, six not knowns with no unit supplied, fifty-three requests and fifty-three section-nine notes, five bodies at the node, nineteen fetchings of the man of about seventy, the seventh column at forty-six and unread and six blanks with nothing at the head of them for four years, the compost line paid at one hundred pounds and sixteen not discharged in sixteen, the leak at three-quarters of an inch with three reasons and no fourth, the beat unlogged and its column unopened, **four** day-and-not-the-figure entries, the aggregate at fifty-three days, **the rota at fifty-two mornings in force, twenty-nine taken and twenty-three not**, and **the series at fifty-five figures on fifty-five mornings with not one of them the same as any of the other fifty-four**, and nobody has said the word steady and nobody has said the word pattern.
