And then four lines, and they are these: the corridor in the pan is open and open is not a road, the vault is under, the ring of bare ground is not walked and not measured and is not going to be this season, whose order it is has been asked four times and answered never; the eleventh figure and the direction and the duration are still on a page with nothing against them, a number off a tinned-iron plate in a building with no roof is not a line to any of those three, the sixth column is blank on eleven of ninety-one rows and the return that lists them is not enclosed, and the second word of the fifth line of that covenant may be there and he has not looked to find out; and a key for one valve is under a cloth on the middle table of a seed house, and the first of next month is six days off, and the well house door is nine hundred yards off and stands at forty-six, and the man of about seventy has been fetched nineteen times and has never once asked which number and neither has anybody else; **and that is two things this holding is not doing, and the list of things it is not doing is longer than the list of things it has done, and the line the question is on is entered and not filled, and I did not write on it, and nobody did.**

# VOLUME 06 — THE CLOSE — Chapters 246–294, days 451–505: WHAT THE CLOSE CHANGED ON THE PAGE

**THE CLOSE REPAIRED FORTY-THREE DEFECTS AT SIXTY-SIX SITES ACROSS TWENTY-EIGHT CHAPTERS IN FOUR BATCHES, AND TOUCHED NONE OF BATCH 0005. TWENTY-EIGHT CHAPTER FILES CHANGED, SIXTY-SIX LINES. THE VOLUME WENT FROM 146,736 TO 146,858 WORDS AND THE MANUSCRIPT FROM 884,101 TO 884,223, AND THE WHOLE OF THE PLUS 122 IS THE CLOSE'S OWN WORK. THE FINDINGS ARE `reviews/volume-06.findings.md`; THE FULL RECORD IS `state/continuity.md` UNDER *VOLUME 06 — THE CLOSE*; THE THREAD POSITION IS `state/open-threads.md` UNDER *State after the Volume 06 close*. BATCH 0005'S OWN PER-CHAPTER SUMMARIES ARE ABOVE THIS SECTION AND NOTHING IN THEM CHANGED.**

### THE TWENTY-EIGHT CHAPTERS, ONE LINE EACH, AND WHAT CHANGED IN EACH

- **Ch 251 —** the man of the north row with the cough was entered as having stood in a yard on the fourth, which put the volume's yards series a step out from Batch 0002's opening figures of twenty-two, twenty-three and twenty-four. He was at the gate, not the yard. 2,667 to 2,669.

# VOLUME 06 — THE THIRD PASS — THE NINE CHAPTERS THE CLOSE PASSES LEFT WRONG, AND WHAT WAS DONE TO THEM

**THE THIRD PASS ON VOLUME 06 REPAIRED NINE CHAPTERS IN PROSE AND THE ENTRIES BELOW ARE CORRECTED IN PLACE RATHER THAN LEFT STANDING AS *CHANGED BY NOBODY*, BECAUSE AN ENTRY THAT SAYS A KNOWN DEFECT WAS NOT REPAIRED IS A LIE WITHIN A SEASON. NOTHING BELOW REWRITES A SCENE, A BEAT, A DAY OR AN OUTCOME; EVERY ENTRY IS A FIGURE, A COUNT, A DAY OR A MONTH FRAME, AND NOT ONE WORD OF ANY OTHER KIND WAS TOUCHED.**

**`chapter-0249.md` — LINE 57, *FOURTEEN* TO *THIRTEEN*. The man of about fifty's own per-speaking count is now monotone across the volume: thirteen here, fourteen at Ch 251, fifteen at Ch 256, and thirty-nine at Ch 294. Ch 251 was not touched, and it is the site that establishes the duplicate. 3,116 words, unchanged.**

**`chapter-0259.md` — NOT TOUCHED, AND THE FINDING THAT NAMED IT NAMED SOMETHING THAT IS NOT THERE.** This chapter carries no `Entered` block at all, and its only reference to another month is the wage of the twenty-first of the third month, which is day 441, in closed Volume 05, and which is not checkable from inside Volume 06. **`chapter-0262.md` — LINE 23, *OF LAST MONTH* TO *OF THIS MONTH*. THE CLERK'S BLOCK WAS NOT TOUCHED AND WAS NEVER A DEFECT: it names the eighteenth of this month and the first of this month, and both are correct.**

# VOLUME 07 — BATCH 0001, CHAPTERS 295–304, DAYS 506–515, MOVEMENT 1: *WHAT HAS TO BE ASKED* (drafted)

**295. Two Hundred And Six** (day 506, Monday, the twenty-sixth of the fifth, 2,800 words)
The volume opens on the **fourth** line of the rota, empty for the twenty-fourth time, the fields above Marden waiting, and the rota at **fifty-three mornings in force, twenty-nine taken, twenty-four not**, and nobody blamed for a field that waited. The third launder carries **644**, the fifty-sixth figure in a series that has not repeated itself, risen, and the aggregate of the four bodies of households has not moved in **fifty-four** days. The day-minus rules are read out loud in about four people, **440 and 487**, the drawer not opened, and the reason is that a man counting a thing every nine days for a month needs two figures of the same shape to know the month has not moved under him. The use log stands at **fifteen** and the reason is not given again in a season. In the seed house with the door shut, the copy of the ledger is on the middle table with the **ninety-one rows, five columns with heads and a sixth with nothing at the head of it, blank on eleven**, and the **five rows on line 41 are not corrected a second time**. The record of the **twenty-fourth ninth-day return** comes in from the previous afternoon: **TWO HUNDRED AND SIX HUNDREDWEIGHT**, the **fourteenth name-pair in eleven years**, read out and read back and read one at a time by each of the four bodies of households where they could see the dial, the **second rule blank for the eighth time**, reconciled twice off one hundred and eighty-four plus twenty-two and off one hundred and ninety-five plus eleven, and the run of eleven held for six figures and entered as a run and not a cause. **The seventh column stands at forty-six and is not read.** Nobody thanked. **Change:** the volume's first figure is on a page, and this holding's oldest standing is read out whole in a month that has turned. **Cost:** twenty-four fields waited, and the only number anybody in that room had been carrying for six weeks was on a sheet that came in the post.

**296. Sacks And No Figure** (day 507, Tuesday, the twenty-seventh, 2,819 words)
First line of the rota, worked; **643**, the fifty-seventh figure, fallen; the aggregate at **fifty-five** days. **Tova Reed describes a seed store from the inside** — thirty feet by twenty, stone floor, split-wood roof against the south embankment, boards at chest height, sacks stood on their ends and counted **in sacks and out loud** by the people who keep it, a second room for paper, a third dark room that was not opened and was not asked for — and she has stood in it twice in twenty days and put her hand on the sacks. **The man of about fifty asks for the number and is refused**, the reason given first: a number carried out of a room gets into a second book in about four days and then has a road nobody can check. **There is no figure of that store in this holding's book and there is not going to be one, and the count of questions the reader of this body has asked anybody in that line is nil and is nil.** **Two units are on a page, sacks and days, and neither is converted into the other, and the cost of what is being discussed is priced in the conversion and the conversion is not being done.** A person who was not asked to look at the stack on the middle table looked at it, and the cloth was not moved, and the count of people who have looked at the thing under it goes to two. **THE FIRST TERM** is put on the table in Tova Reed's hand: *NO CONVERSION*. The man of about fifty writes the word **none** in his column with a date and a reason in one line and four ruled lines under it. Nobody thanked. **Change:** a figure this holding has never had, refused by the man who keeps columns, and a public term that prices a thing in the unit it is paid in. **Cost:** a column with a word in it and no figure, kept honestly.

The reader of this body asks one question with the reason first, and **the count of questions he has asked him goes from three to four, in a room with the door shut and not in a yard**. The word is **work done**, and the reason it is that word is that the moment anybody changes it the fact goes out of it. **THE SECOND TERM** goes on the table beside the first, unsmoothed: a thing that connects two places is not finished until the people at the far end have been asked and have answered, and a thing that cannot be undone by a refusal is a pipe. **The two terms are read side by side and they do not agree**, and the first can be satisfied by a refusal and the second cannot, and the fen enters both and does not enter which is right. The man of about fifty leaves the table with two things on it and no third. **The man of the north row with the cough is not in the room and was not asked to be in it and was not asked to hold anything.** Nobody thanked. **Change:** the count of questions is four and the far end has a term and a voice. **Cost:** a walk of about four miles and a half each way in one day by a man who was not paid and not thanked.

**299. The Thirtieth And A Reading** (day 510, Friday, the thirtieth, 2,904 words)
Fourth line, empty, **twenty-five fields waited**, the rota at **fifty-four in force, twenty-nine taken, twenty-five not**. **650**, the sixtieth figure, risen; the aggregate at **fifty-eight** days. The man of about fifty says, giving the reason first, that he has written on that door four times in four years without being asked, and that **a column's job is to hold a number and not to explain itself**, and that a person in four years reading forty-eight without knowing what it was about is the correct outcome. **The man of about seventy is not fetched** and the twentieth is available tomorrow and nobody asks him anything about it. First line, worked. **THE MONTH TURNED IN THE NIGHT AND THE COUNT DID NOT RESET: the figure is 648, the sixty-first, and a series that has run sixty mornings without a repeat does not begin again because a calendar did it.** In twenty-eight days since the third of last month the series has risen nineteen times and fallen nine times. The reader of this body asks one question in that yard, *if you wrote one, would you know what to put in it*, and the answer is two words, and he entered that he knew what he was doing when he asked. A second board on the far side of that building carries four headed columns with paint over paint, and a board will be soft through at the bottom nail in about nine years, and neither argument answers the other. ### THE THREE THINGS A BATCH 0004 WRITER MUST KNOW

**FIRST, THE DAY-MINUS HABIT RESTARTED AND THE COUNT IS ON THE PAGE MORNING BY MORNING. He last read the pair out loud on the twelfth of this month and began again on the seventeenth, and the pages are consistent: the seventeenth after four mornings without, the eighteenth the second morning running, the nineteenth the first morning since he started again that he did not say them, the twentieth two mornings out of the four, the twenty-first four out of the five, the twenty-second four out of the six, the twenty-third five out of the seven, the twenty-fourth five out of the eight, and the twenty-fifth six out of the nine. A LATER WRITER SUBTRACTS OR READS THE LAST LINE AND DOES NOT CARRY A COUNT ACROSS THE MONTH TURN WITHOUT NAMING THE MORNING HE RESTARTED ON.**

**SECOND, THE MAN OF THE NORTH ROW WITH THE COUGH IS NOT IN ANY OF THE TEN CHAPTERS. The far end of the connection on the eighteenth is a person holding a pattern for four who is not the reader of this body, and the chapter says so and does not name him and does not put him in a room and does not print his two counts of twenty-seven yards and ten silences, and both are unmoved. THE COUNT OF THE TIMES HE HAS OFFERED TO BE SOMEWHERE HE IS NOT THE ENGINEER OF RECORD FOR IS **HARLAN VETCH’S** AND IS TWO AND IS NOT PRINTED HERE. A LATER WRITER WHO NEEDS IT GOES TO `chapter-0287.md:45` AND PRINTS HARLAN VETCH’S NAME ON IT.**

**THIRD, THE COUNT OF THE TIMES THE MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-ONE OF SILLING HAS BROUGHT THAT BARROW UP THAT ROAD STANDS AT ELEVEN AND WAS RESTATED AND NOT RAISED AT Ch 321. The two times on that road stand where they stood: about an hour and a quarter, Harlan Vetch’s, and about an hour and three-quarters, the man of about thirty-one of Silling’s own.**

### THE FAULT BATCH 0003 FOUND IN ITS OWN PROMPT, NAMED

**THE PROMPT'S FIGURE FOR THE TWENTY-SEVENTH RETURN WAS WRONG AGAINST ITS OWN ARITHMETIC.** It said *one hundred and thirty-nine hundredweight, being two hundred and twenty-eight plus eleven*, and two hundred and twenty-eight plus eleven is **two hundred and thirty-nine**. `chapter-0312.md:19` and `:55` put the twenty-sixth at **two hundred and twenty-eight hundredweight** and derive it twice, off two hundred and seventeen plus eleven and off one hundred and ninety-five plus thirty-three, so the next in the run is two hundred and thirty-nine and the second arithmetic is one hundred and ninety-five plus forty-four. **WITHDRAWN, ALL THREE FORMS, AND NOT MERELY OVERWRITTEN: *one hundred and thirty-nine hundredweight*, *being two hundred and twenty-eight plus eleven*, and the chapter title *One Hundred And Thirty-Nine*. Ch 321 now prints TWO HUNDRED AND THIRTY-NINE in six places, the title included, and derives it twice. The next return is day 541 at two hundred and fifty and the one after is day 550 at two hundred and sixty-one, and both agree with the outline's own list.**

The day-minus pair is read out loud, four hundred and seventy-two and five hundred and nineteen, eight mornings out of the twelve. The man of about thirty-one of Silling is at the second gate all morning and the fen enters that a gate is a gate and not a boundary and that the count of fields to mornings was nineteen and nineteen until the fourth line began coming round on mornings this holding has nobody free for. In the room: **about four people have copied the five terms out by hand and nobody was asked for a copy and nobody gave one**, the man of about fifty checked two of them against the drawer and they agree. Tova Reed speaks without the reason first and the fen enters that she did not and the count does not move. **The reader of this body gives no reason before what he says, and the fen has entered that he gave none, and no figure is printed for him.**

**328. Nine Acres, Twenty-Ninth** (day 539, Saturday, the twenty-ninth; first line worked; ~2,792 words)
**Six hundred and eighty-five**, the eighty-ninth, fallen. The first line is the boundary ditch and the two culverts on the Marden side, and about eleven people are working ground this holding has never held about nine feet away from about four people working a ditch it has held for eleven years, and nobody speaks across. At about the third hour **the nine acres of Marden come off** and the gate is shut from the Marden side at about half past three by the person who is allowed to shut it, and nobody in this holding asked her to and nobody was on the ground. The woman of about thirty-eight of Marden says, the reason first: the decision of the eleventh of a month two months back is not reopened, a bridge existing does not reopen it, the key is in her hand and has not been used, and she says the fifteen words of the holding's own decision without improving them. **The reader of this body asks her nothing, and the count of questions he has asked her is nil and is nil, and the fen says out loud that he would rather it were written down than read.** **Change:** nine acres of somebody's own ground come off and the holding takes nothing and gets no figure for it.

**329. Forty-Nine** (day 540, Sunday, the thirtieth; second line worked; ~2,788 words)
**Six hundred and ninety-one**, the ninetieth, risen. The day-minus pair is read out loud, four hundred and seventy-four and five hundred and twenty-one, nine mornings out of the fourteen. At about the third hour **the seventh column of the well house door is read to forty-nine**, the third such pair of consecutive reading days begins, the door is described as an object, and the six other columns have nothing at the head of them and nobody writes a heading on one. The man of about thirty-one of Silling says out loud that he has started to be a person who goes up there rather than a person who is sent, and that he will be there in the morning for the other half of the pair and that nobody is going to write that down. The man of about fifty works out that the pair has happened three times in four years and does not write the three down. **The reader of this body announces the four things that fall on tomorrow's morning, the reason first, so that they arrive in a book with a day on it before they arrive in a yard.**

**330. The Month Turns** (day 541, Monday, **the first of the seventh**; third line worked; ~2,936 words)
**The month turns in the night and the count of the series does not reset: ninety-first, and it was ninetieth yesterday.** **Six hundred and eighty-seven**, fallen, thirty-four rises and twenty-four falls in fifty-eight days. **FOUR CLOCKS FALL ON THIS MORNING AND ON NO OTHER IN THE TEN.** The compost line at the second hour, PAID, one hundred pounds, **the run at eighteen not discharged in eighteen**, and it is not a measurement of the ground. The **seventh column read again and standing at fifty**, the other half of the third pair. **The man of about seventy fetched for the twenty-first time**, asked nothing, and no person in this holding has said why and the fen is not going to. And at a place five days east, the **twenty-eighth ninth-day return at two hundred and fifty hundredweight, the eighteenth name-pair in eleven years, the second rule left blank for the twelfth time**, reconciled twice off two hundred and thirty-nine plus eleven and off one hundred and ninety-five plus fifty-five, the run of eleven having held for ten figures, **the eleven-above derivation used and not refused and said so on the page**. Harlan Vetch holds the fifth share and has held it eleven years and thirty-five days, and the barrow count stands at eleven and is not raised. In the room: **a bridge is not a mark, a headache is not a mark, and the mark being hot is not a mark**, the mark is four inches and branches twice, the four accounts stand at four. **Change:** the month turns on a morning that pays for itself, and nothing in it is an answer.

**331. Refused On The Ground** (day 542, Tuesday, the second; **fourth, nobody, 33**; ~2,740 words)
The fourth line comes round empty for the thirty-third time, the fields wait the thirty-third, and the rota stands at sixty-two mornings in force, twenty-nine taken and thirty-three not, being twenty-nine and thirty-three. **Six hundred and ninety-four**, the ninety-second, risen, thirty-five rises and twenty-four falls in fifty-nine days. The day-minus pair is read out loud, four hundred and seventy-six and five hundred and twenty-three, ten mornings out of the sixteen. **At a place five days east the man of about thirty-one of Silling stands at the edge of the ring of bare ground and refuses a road**, having priced the straight line across it at about **a day and a half of walking**, and the pricing came off two lines on the back of a sheet drawn by a man who has never been on the ring, and neither line goes across it. **The ring is not walked and not measured and not crossed and not priced by walking it and not explained**, and it is entered that the ground inside is about nine inches lower at the middle and that nobody put a level on it. The man of about fifty declines to give the saving a column: a saving is a figure that only exists if somebody is walking the long way. **The reader of this body says out loud that he is not reaching for a thing in this holding's books and does not name it**, and that a refusal is a thing a person is entitled to make, and that he has not got a view about why the ring is bare and is not going to acquire one in about four years.

**332. A Warden In A Room** (day 543, Wednesday, the third; first line worked; ~2,791 words)
**Six hundred and ninety**, the ninety-third, fallen, and in sixty days the series has risen thirty-five times and fallen twenty-five times. The day-minus pair is not read out loud, ten mornings out of the seventeen. **WARDEN PIKE IS IN A ROOM ONCE**, the president of the Rootwright Assembly, on his own account and not sent for, and not on the roll for the district the line stands in. **He says both halves in one speech: that a connection carries whatever is at the other end of it, which is true and is what the blight inside the inhabited line and fifteen days of a running connection have left this holding unable to argue with, and that he signed an order sealing the route anyway and does not think he had the right to.** He does not give a reason first and the count of that is not in this holding's history. He signs, and the paper is entered whole and is not one of the three documents in the drawer.

> **AN ORDER OF THE ROOTWRIGHT ASSEMBLY, SEALING THE ROUTE BETWEEN THE FIELD GATE AND THE THORNWILD EDGE AGAINST ALL WORK AND ALL PASSING UNTIL AN ASSEMBLY IS CONVENCED THAT THE GROUND BEYOND IT MAY BE USED. SIGNED AT THE FOOT IN INK: H. Pike, President.**

He leaves and does not ask to be thanked and nobody thanks him. **The reader of this body will not answer whether an order like that is one the people at both ends of it are entitled to refuse, and says on the page that the answer is not his and that standing in the middle of that question would answer it.** **Change:** the route is sealed by a valid instrument and nothing is closed.

**333. Said In A Yard** (day 544, Thursday, the fourth; second line worked; ~2,777 words)
**Six hundred and ninety-seven**, the ninety-fourth, risen, thirty-six rises and twenty-five falls in sixty-one days, and it is the highest figure in four volumes of this series. The day-minus pair is read out loud, four hundred and seventy-eight and five hundred and twenty-five, eleven mornings out of the eighteen. At about the sixth hour, in the yard of the seed house, in about five people, **a name is said out loud in a yard for the first time in this holding** — by the man of about fifty, in the middle of an ordinary sentence about the west dyke, and he was not asked to say it and did not know, and the reader of this body heard all of it and did not move. **The count of that is one, it is entered where it happened, in the yard and not in a room, and it is one and not two.** Nothing wrong was said, so the count of things said out loud in a yard and got wrong stands at five and did not move. **The count of things a person who keeps a book in this holding has said in a yard that the engineer of record had not thought of goes twelve to thirteen**, and the page says the two counts are two counts and neither is added to the other. The man of about fifty says he is not going to say it again, because a name said once in a yard in four years is a thing and a name said twice is a habit. **Change:** the one thing this volume had left to spend is spent, and nothing was settled by it.

**334. The Terms, Read Back** (day 545, Friday, the fifth; third line worked; ~2,846 words)
**Six hundred and ninety-three**, the ninety-fifth, fallen, thirty-six rises and twenty-six falls in sixty-two days. The day-minus pair is not read out loud, eleven mornings out of the nineteen. **The five terms are read back in about nine people and improved in no part, and the one that is the man of about fifty's is not improved either**, and the refusal of it stands and the term is not withdrawn, and both are true in the same room. **The copy of the ledger comes off the shelf: ninety-one rows, five columns with heads and a sixth with nothing at the head of it, blank on eleven of the ninety-one, the eleven counted off in about nine people with seven of them not on line 41, the district return that lists them not enclosed and never seen by anybody in this holding, the five rows on line 41 not corrected a second time, and the sixth column still headed nothing with nobody writing a heading on it.** Tova Reed, Soren Rill, the man of about fifty and the reader of this body each give the reason first, and the woman of about thirty-eight of Marden reads the third of the five out WITHOUT the reason first, so her own count does not move and stands at seventeen, and nobody asked her a question. **THE BATCH ENDS ON A MORNING ON WHICH THE CONNECTION HAS BEEN RUNNING SEVENTEEN DAYS AND HAS NOT BEEN CLOSED AND NOBODY IN THIS HOLDING CAN SAY WHO IS HOLDING THE OTHER END OF IT**, and the order sealing the route is two days old in a drawer and nobody has been asked whether it is one that may be refused.

### THE FIGURES BATCH 0004 OWED THE READER, AND WHERE EACH ONE IS

1. **Five terms written in about nine people and one of the five in the man of about fifty's own hand, improved in no part and not asked to be improved: Ch 325.** The other four are Tova Reed's and Soren Rill's.
2. **Tova Reed and Soren Rill refuse the fifth of the five in a room, the reason first in both, the refusal stands, nobody improved a word of the term or of the refusal: Ch 326.**
3. **The fourth line empty for the thirty-second time and the thirty-third, the fields waiting thirty-two and thirty-three, and the rota at sixty-one and sixty-two mornings in force: Ch 327 and Ch 331.** 29 + 32 = 61 and 29 + 33 = 62, and twenty-nine taken did not move on any of the ten mornings.
4. **The nine acres of Marden come off on the twenty-ninth and the decision of the eleventh of a month two months back is not reopened, the key is not used, nothing goes in the two-foot gap, and the count of questions asked of the woman of about thirty-eight of Marden is nil and is nil: Ch 328.**
5. **The seventh column read to forty-nine on the thirtieth and to fifty on the first, the third such pair in four years, and the six other columns headed nothing: Ch 329 and Ch 330.**
6. **Four clocks on one morning and no other: Ch 330.** The column, the twenty-first fetching of the man of about seventy, the compost line at eighteen not discharged in eighteen, and the twenty-eighth return at two hundred and fifty with the second rule blank for the twelfth time.
7. **The shortcut priced at about a day and a half and refused from the edge of the ring, which is not walked, not measured, not crossed and not explained: Ch 331.**
8. **Warden Pike in a room once, right about a danger and wrong about who decides, both halves in one speech, and an order sealing the route signed `H. Pike, President`: Ch 332.**
9. **The engineer's name said out loud in a yard once, by a person who was not asked to and did not know, the count of that is one and does not go to two, and the count of things said in a yard and got wrong does not move: Ch 333.**
10. **The five terms read back and improved in no part, the eleven blank rows counted off with seven not on line 41, the district return not in the room, the sixth column still headed nothing, the five rows on line 41 not corrected again, and the connection running seventeen days with nobody able to say who holds the other end: Ch 334.**

### THE TWO THINGS A BATCH 0005 WRITER MUST KNOW, AND BOTH OF THEM ARE FIGURES

**FIRST, THE CONNECTION IS SEVENTEEN DAYS OLD ON DAY 545 AND THE COUNT IS DAY MINUS FIVE HUNDRED AND TWENTY-EIGHT, NOT A STANDING FIGURE, BEING EIGHTEEN ON DAY 546 AND TWENTY-EIGHT ON DAY 556. **THE FORM *DAY MINUS FOUR HUNDRED AND THIRTEEN* IS WITHDRAWN AND WAS WRONG: four hundred and thirteen is not a day in this series and a writer who subtracts it lands on a morning the connection was not running.** It was made on the eighteenth of the second month, being day 528, and `chapter-0324.md:15` prints seven days on the twenty-fifth of that month and 535 minus 528 is seven, and 545 minus 528 is seventeen. `chapter-0331.md:51` prints fourteen on the second of the seventh and 542 minus 528 is fourteen, `chapter-0332.md:47` prints fifteen and 543 minus 528 is fifteen, and the same run is on the page morning by morning. A LATER WRITER SUBTRACTS AND DOES NOT CARRY A COUNT ACROSS THE BATCH BOUNDARY.**

**SECOND, THE CLIMAX HOLDS THE FAR END FOR ABOUT NINE MINUTES AND IT IS NOT IN THIS BATCH. **The man of the north row with the cough is in none of these ten chapters, his two counts of twenty-seven yards and ten silences are unmoved and unprinted, and the minutes of a connection enter neither count. The count of times he has offered to be somewhere he is not the engineer of record for is **HARLAN VETCH'S**, at `chapter-0287.md:45`, and is two, and is not printed here. A LATER WRITER WHO NEEDS IT GOES TO THAT LINE AND PRINTS HARLAN VETCH'S NAME ON IT.**

### THE TWO FAULTS BATCH 0004 FOUND, AND BOTH ARE NAMED

**FIRST, THE CARD'S *FOURTEEN DAYS* IS WITHDRAWN AND THE PAGE'S *SEVENTEEN* STANDS.** The card for 334 said the batch ends on a morning on which the connection has been running for **fourteen** days, and fourteen is the figure for the second of the seventh, being day 542, and the last morning of this batch is the fifth of that month, being day 545. **`chapter-0324.md:15` prints seven days on day 535 for a connection made on day 528, and 535 minus 528 is seven, so the figure is a subtraction and not a list, and seven plus the ten mornings from the twenty-sixth of the second month to the fifth of the seventh is seventeen.** Ch 334 prints seventeen in four places, in the prose, in the closing paragraph and twice in the clerk's block. **A WRITER WHO TAKES THE CARD GETS FOURTEEN AND IS LOW BY THREE AGAINST A CONNECTION HE HAS READ ON THE PAGE FOUR TIMES IN THIS BATCH ALONE.**

**SECOND, SIX HUNDRED AND EIGHTY-SEVEN IS ALSO ON THE PAGE AT `chapter-0190.md:43`, IN A DIFFERENT UNIT, A DIFFERENT SENTENCE AND A DIFFERENT VOLUME, AND IT IS NOT A COLLISION.** It stands there as **six hundred and eighty-seven pounds and a half** of water against a foot, inside a paragraph about the head of a channel in the fourth month of the second year. The third launder is a hundredweight series and this is a pressure in pounds, and this is the same situation as the six hundred hundredweight at `chapter-0247.md:33` and the declined figure of one hundred and twenty-seven at `chapter-0285.md:37`, **and the series rule is a rule about hundredweight in the third launder and not about every integer in the manuscript.** The other nine figures of this batch were checked by script against all 334 files on disk with a word boundary and appear in their own chapter and nowhere else. **NAMED RATHER THAN SILENTLY PASSED, BECAUSE A FIGURE THAT IS ONLY OVERWRITTEN COMES BACK.**

# State after Volume 07 Batch 0005 (Chapters 335-343, days 546-556) - THE CLIMAX AND THE RESOLUTION, *THE BRIDGE BELOW*

**Volume 07 IS WRITTEN.** Batch 0005 is Chapters 335 to 343 on days 546 to 556, nine chapters across eleven days, with Chapters 338 and 340 each carrying two days and no morning claimed twice and none left unnarrated. It is the last batch of Volume 07. It carries the volume's climax and its resolution together and it takes **ZERO `Entered` BLOCKS IN ALL NINE CHAPTERS**, which is the inverse of Volume 06's Batch 0005, which carried eight. The batch is at 26,460 words across nine chapters after its review fix pass, being 2,975 / 3,047 / 2,880 / 2,969 / 2,939 / 3,040 / 2,847 / 2,828 / 2,935, and the Volume 07 bracket closes at 140,227 across five of five batches and the manuscript at 1,024,475 across 343 chapters. **Three sentences and one paragraph of the nine were repaired in that pass and the repairs are in the governing record at the foot of `state/continuity.md`: the two-foot gap is at the node end of the eleven hundred and is no longer standing at the field gate, and the four-mile barrow road and the five-mile cart road to the node are two roads and the chapter says so.** The figures 26,398, 140,165 and 1,024,413 are withdrawn.

## THE NINE CHAPTERS, ONE LINE EACH

1. **335 (day 546, Saturday, the sixth), *A Window, And The Long Way Round*.** The fourth line came round and was empty for the thirty-fourth time, the fields waited, the rota stands at sixty-three in force, twenty-nine taken and thirty-four not, and the office's window of work opens on the sixth and shuts on the eleventh. The route for the bridge is settled the long way round in a room, with the reason first, by the man of about thirty-one of Silling standing at nothing, and the ring is not walked and not measured and not explained. Tova Reed says out loud that the seed under the cloth is not being opened and that the not opening is theirs and not the office's. The reader of this body says out loud that he is the near end and that he is not going to pick the far one. A deliberate gap is written on the day sheet where the day and a half of walking would have gone, dated, with no why on it. Nobody thanked anybody.
2. **336 (day 547, Sunday, the seventh), *Two Ends, And Two People*.** The first line was worked. The reader of this body walks half a mile to the north row in the wet and does not ask the man of the north row with the cough whether he will; he tells him which end he is and asks him three questions about furniture, and is given a stone sill, a board out of the cart shed, and a third thing, which is to put his hand on a table palm up and not look at it. Three inches on the right forearm that do not branch, permanent, entered in his own hand on a sheet of his own that nobody reads. The man of the north row with the cough arranges not to be thanked in advance and says the nine minutes are a figure about a bridge and not an answer to what he will be able to do in about four years. The count of yards and the count of silences are named and neither moves. Nobody thanked anybody.
3. **337 (day 548, Monday, the eighth), *Sacks, And Four Days*.** The second line was worked, the west dyke. Soren Rill brings a board off a rack in the store at Thornwild with a number of sacks on it in a hand about six inches high, and nobody in the holding asked for it, and the count of questions the reader of this body has asked anybody in that line is nil and it is nil. What the sacks cost is about four days of seed and not a weight, and the four days and the sacks are not converted into one another, and NO CONVERSION is applied to something for the first time in a month. The man of about thirty-one of Silling says the sacks come along in loads at barrow speed over roots and that the count of loads is not a figure this holding keeps. The woman of about thirty-eight of Marden is in the room, speaks without the reason first, and her count does not move.
4. **338 (days 549 and 550, Tuesday and Wednesday, the ninth and the tenth), *Two Days, And A Number That Goes In*.** The third line was worked on the ninth. The four of the five terms on the table go across to Thornwild in the inside of a coat, and the second of the five, withdrawn and not unwithdrawn, goes with them, and nobody adds a sixth and nobody dates the back of one. The near end is put at about nine feet inside the field gate facing the wall of the second house. The fourth line came round on the tenth and was empty for the thirty-fifth time, the rota stands at sixty-four, and the day-minus pair is read out loud at the node for the first time this month at a place that is not the seed house. **THE TWENTY-NINTH NINTH-DAY RETURN GOES IN AT TWO HUNDRED AND SIXTY-ONE ON A STEELYARD IN A BUILDING WITH NO ROOF, BEING THE NINETEENTH NAME-PAIR IN ELEVEN YEARS, RECONCILED TWICE OFF TWO HUNDRED AND FIFTY PLUS ELEVEN AND OFF ONE HUNDRED AND NINETY-FIVE PLUS SIXTY-SIX, AND THE CHAPTER SAYS ON THE PAGE THAT THIS HOLDING IS USING THAT DERIVATION AND IS NOT REFUSING IT. THE SECOND RULE IS LEFT BLANK FOR THE THIRTEENTH TIME. Harlan Vetch has held the fifth share eleven years and forty-four days; the count of times the man of about thirty-one of Silling has brought that barrow up that road is eleven and is not raised.**
5. **339 (day 551, Thursday, the eleventh), *The Eleventh, And It Shuts*.** The first line was worked. **THE WINDOW OF THE OFFICE'S WORK SHUTS ON THIS MORNING, IT WAS OPEN SIX DAYS, NO WORK IS CARRIED OUT OF IT, IT IS NOT EXTENDED, AND NO WINDOW HAS EVER BEEN EXTENDED IN A SEASON.** A rider brings a sheet on district paper from a district and not from the office named at the head of the memorandum, saying no, and saying no correctly, and every particular of it is right. The man of about fifty puts the sheet in the drawer face up and says out loud that what came back last time came back in four days as a form and not as an instrument. Tova Reed says the office has said no and was right to and that nobody is going to ask for an extension. The reader of this body says he is not going to say the word offer in that room. At about the ninth hour he goes and stands against the wall at the field gate and times himself three times and once more without writing it down, and does not put it in a book.
6. **340 (days 552 and 553, Friday and Saturday, the twelfth and the thirteenth), *The Bridge Below*.** The second line was worked on the twelfth. **THE BRIDGE RUNS. THE NEAR END IS HELD BY THE READER OF THIS BODY, THE FAR END BY THE MAN OF THE NORTH ROW WITH THE COUGH, AND IT IS ABOUT NINE MINUTES, AND NOBODY THANKS HIM AND HE IS NOT ASKED TO BE.** It is told from the near end only. What arrives in the four inches on the inside of his own forearm is the weight of a body on a board, the cold of a right hand that has been against cold stone, three coughs, and, at about the eighth minute, the moment a body stops being able to get itself off a thing. He put his hand down and did not press it. The man of about fifty stands about nine feet off with a day sheet and says one sentence. The man of about thirty-one of Silling, the only person at the far end who could have said what happened, is not asked. **THE STORE PAYS ABOUT FOUR DAYS OF SEED FOR IT AND THE FOUR DAYS ARE NOT RETURNED AND THE SACKS ARE NOT CONVERTED INTO THE DAYS.** The thirteenth is the first of the three mornings the bridge stands with nobody in charge of it, and there is a hollow in the beaten ground with a leaf in it and nothing in this holding that can say whether it is on.
7. **341 (day 554, Sunday, the fourteenth), *Claimed, Correctly*.** The fourth line came round and was empty for the thirty-sixth time, the fields waited, the rota stands at sixty-five, and twenty-nine and thirty-six are sixty-five. A sheet claims the corridor between the field gate and the Thornwild edge as a work of the Crown Engine, in a printed table with four columns, and it is correct in every particular and it is not a form and it is not an instrument. **ONE OF THE FOUR BODIES OF HOUSEHOLDS DECLINES A SECOND TIME, IN A ROOM, WITH THE REASON GIVEN FIRST: SILLING DECLINES THE CORRIDOR AND DOES NOT DECLINE THE BRIDGE, AND NOBODY IMPROVES THE DECLINE AND IT IS NOT WRITTEN DOWN.** The man of about thirty-one of Silling asks out loud, for the second time, whether an order a warden signed is a thing the people at both ends of a bridge may say no to, and the man of about fifty and the reader of this body both decline to answer it and neither refusal is the last word on it.
8. **342 (day 555, Monday, the fifteenth), *Rejected As Offered*.** The first line was worked. It is the third of the three mornings the bridge stands with nobody in charge of it, and the hollow has a leaf in it, and nobody in the holding has asked anybody at the far end whether it is there. **SOREN RILL WALKS FOUR MILES AND A HALF IN THE RAIN AND SAYS THAT THE ASSEMBLY AT THORNWILD TOOK THE FIVE OF THEM AS OFFERED, READ THEM OUT, IMPROVED NO PART OF ANY OF THEM, WITHDREW NO PART OF ANY OF THEM, AND DECLINED ALL FIVE; THAT IT DECLINED THEM BECAUSE DECLINING WAS THE ONLY THING AVAILABLE TO ANYBODY IN THAT ROOM; THAT IT DID NOT SAY WHICH ONE AND HE IS NOT GOING TO; AND THAT NOTHING CAME BACK IN HIS COAT.** The man of about fifty enters three lines and no fifth. The reader of this body asks him nothing and says on the page that the two units are still sacks and days.
9. **343 (day 556, Tuesday, the sixteenth), *A Corridor, Under Vetoes*.** The second line was worked. **THE ORDINARY READING OF THE WELL ON THE SHELF IS ENTERED AS A DAY AND NOT A FIGURE, AND THE COUNT OF ENTRIES IN THIS HOLDING'S BOOK THAT CARRY A DAY AND NO FIGURE GOES FROM FIVE TO SIX, WITH NO ORDINAL, NO FIGURE, NO GUESS AND NO QUESTION ASKED OF ANYBODY AT THAT FAR END IN ELEVEN YEARS.** A form arrives from an office whose business is a register of persons who may set a sequence against a valve; it is read out whole in the one capitalised block in the whole of the batch, it is not filled, it is a different document from the form with four lines, and it goes on the table and not into the drawer. The man of the north row with the cough is given no figure in the shared sentence and the chapter says so. **A MIGRATION AND TRADE CORRIDOR OPENS ANYWAY UNDER LOCAL VETOES**, in about nine people, in a holding with no charter, over ground nobody has spoken for, under the refusal of a body of households that has not been withdrawn and under a decision of a body of households that has not been reopened, and the fifteen words are read out of the drawer and not improved. The man of about thirty-one of Silling asks the warden question a second time and the room does not answer it. Nobody thanked anybody and the last line is not an answer.

IT IS THE CLOSE'S READING NOTE, AND IT IS HERE BECAUSE A CLOSE THAT RECORDS ITS FIGURES ONLY IN `state/continuity.md` HAS RECORDED THEM IN ONE PLACE, AND THIS REPOSITORY HAS ALREADY LOST A FIGURE TO A LAYER THAT AGREED WITH ITSELF.**

**FORTY-NINE CHAPTERS WERE READ IN FULL, IN ORDER, CHAPTERS 295 TO 343, AND THE WORD FIGURE OF EVERY ONE OF THEM WAS RE-MEASURED WITH `wc -w` AFTER THE LAST PROSE EDIT. 140,227 ACROSS FORTY-NINE, AND THE MANUSCRIPT IS 1,024,475 ACROSS 343 WITH NO RESIDUAL.**

3. **386 (day 599, Wednesday, the twenty-ninth of the eighth, the first line) - *One Ear*.** The boundary ditch and the two culverts, six people to the fourth hour, and the far one left alone because it is going down by itself. Launder **803**, a fall; the window at a hundred and sixteen, sixty-three and fifty-three. Aggregate 147, 146 of 148. **The pair at 533 and 580 read aloud, forty-five of seventy-three.** **THE FIFTH SESSION IS ENTERED IN THE PROSE AND NOT AS A BLOCK, at about the fifth hour of the morning, before anything is done, with the four of the four, the purpose, the duration to the fifth hour, the stop signal that is hers and is not entered, and the independent witness who has been told a condition exists and not what it is; under the four he writes ORDER SOUGHT and the hour and rules four lines and nothing goes under them.** The settlement of the twentieth governs it and is not rewritten and not settled a fifth time, and the man of about fifty says why the four lines stay empty without being asked and nobody asked him. **What comes back is the order, in the order the wood keeps things in, and it is not the order of the sheet five miles east and not the order the head of the refused sheet gave them in, and it puts the whole of the small ground at the north end of the pan after the wide branches below the sluice, and it says what and it says when and has no name and no office and no subject on it, and the eight that did not come out of the wood on the twenty-third are not in it and were not guessed at.** **She comes out of that wood with one ear and it is not coming back, and she says it herself on the bank in her own words with the reason first at twenty-five: she can hear and she cannot put a sound on a side, and it is not a wound and not on his arm and not a fifth account, and she is the person who decides when he stops and nobody is going to take the seed work off her.** Nobody said sorry, nobody touched her arm, nobody was comforted, the reader of this body did not ask her a second question, and the not-knowns stay at six.

4. **387 (day 600, Thursday, the thirtieth of the eighth, the second line, the column to fifty-three, and a reading) - *A Day And Not A Figure*.** The two gates and the about six feet of wall, four people, an hour and a quarter, and about two feet of the wall came away in a piece and had to be laid again. Launder **812**, a rise; the window at a hundred and seventeen, sixty-four and fifty-three. Aggregate 148, 147 of 149. **The pair is not read aloud because the man of about fifty had been on a ladder at the well house door since before the sixth hour holding the lamp, and this page carries no figure for the run**; the pair stands at 534 and 581. **THE SEVENTH COLUMN IS READ TO FIFTY-THREE AT NINE HUNDRED YARDS IN ABOUT TWENTY-FIVE PEOPLE AND READ BACK BY THE CLERK, AND IT IS THE FIRST OF THE FIFTH CONSECUTIVE-DAY PAIR IN FOUR YEARS AND THE SECOND OF IT IS TOMORROW, AND FROM THE THIRTETH IT MAY NOT GO BACK TO FIFTY-TWO.** **AND AT ABOUT THE FOURTH HOUR THE WELL ON THAT SHELF IS READ, FOUR HUNDRED MILES AND FOUR DAYS OFF, AND GOES IN AS A DAY AND NOT AS A FIGURE, WITH NO ORDINAL, NO FIGURE AND NO UNIT IN ELEVEN YEARS, TAKING THAT COUNT FROM SEVEN TO EIGHT, THE WALL AT FOURTEEN MARKS GIVING NONE UP, THE FOUR FEET OF SHORTFALL NOT DECOMPOSED, AND NO ENTRY FOR THAT WELL COMING BACK. IT IS THE ONLY CHAPTER OF THE BATCH THAT MAY MENTION IT AND THE OTHER EIGHT DO NOT.** No reason is given before anything this morning and so no figure of the six is printed on the page. The six blank columns have nothing at the head of them.

5. **388 (day 601, Friday, the first of the ninth, the third line, the column to fifty-four, the twenty-third fetching, the compost line) - *Three Clocks And A First*.** The month turns in the night and nothing in the building turns with it. The two places, four people, the second of them empty. Launder **807**, a fall; the window at a hundred and eighteen, sixty-four and fifty-four. Aggregate 149, 148 of 150. **The seventh column is read to fifty-four and read back by the clerk, the second of the fifth pair, and from the first it may not go back to fifty-three.** **The man of about seventy is fetched for the twenty-third time and the count goes off twenty-two onto twenty-three on this morning alone, and nobody asks him anything and nobody ever has, and the man of about fifty enters it with a day and an hour and no question and gives the reason first at 109, which is that a question on that line is a question the man has been asked.** He came on foot with a stick and the appointed person went out with a cart and he was given tea and he looked at the register form for ten minutes and did not ask about it. **The compost line falls at twenty not discharged in twenty with the word paid before the figure.** The pair at 535 and 582 read aloud, forty-six of seventy-five, **and the frame of the run changes here, once, from of a month two months back to of a month three months back, and the boards' own frame changed at the same hour and the two are not interchangeable.**

6. **389 (day 602, Saturday, the second of the ninth, the fourth line, forty-eight) - *Correct In Every Particular*.** Nobody on the headland, the fields wait, the rota rises by exactly one to **seventy-seven in force, twenty-nine taken and forty-eight not**, and **both counts of the rotation are printed, being the twenty-fifth of the run out of the twenty-sixth of a month three months back and the twelfth since the eighteenth of a month two months back, the frame having moved with the month.** Launder **816**, a rise; the window at a hundred and nineteen, sixty-five and fifty-four. Aggregate 150, 149 of 151. **The pair is not read aloud because the man of about fifty had been in the room with the door shut since the fourth hour with three things out on the table, and a pair read in that room would have been a fourth thing on it**; the pair stands at 536 and 583. **THE PROOF IS ASSEMBLED IN ABOUT NINE PEOPLE WITH THE DOOR SHUT OUT OF A STANDING ENTERED IN A ROOM, A SCHEDULE READ OUT OF WOOD, AND THE ORDINARY WORK OF TWO VOLUMES, AND IT HAS THREE PARTS AND ONE GAP: A MAINTENANCE SCHEDULE DOES NOT TAKE A BRANCH OFF ANYTHING; THE ORDER PUTS THE SMALL GROUND AFTER THE WIDE BRANCHES BELOW THE SLUICE AND A MAN KEEPING LINES DOES THE OTHER THING; AND NOTHING ON THE NINETEEN HAS A NAME ON IT. THE GAP IS THAT A WOOD KEEPS ONE ORDER AND THERE IS NO SECOND GROUND TO CHECK IT AGAINST. IT IS INCOMPLETE AND CREDIBLE IN THE SAME BREATH.** **THE CONTAMINATION FRAMING IS PUT IN FRONT OF THE ROOM AS A BOLD DOCUMENT PARAGRAPH AND IS CORRECT IN EVERY PARTICULAR, AND NOBODY IN THAT ROOM SAYS IT IS A LIE AND NOBODY IMPROVES IT, AND THE PAGE SAYS THAT CALLING A CORRECT DOCUMENT A LIE IS THE ONLY MISTAKE ANYBODY COULD MAKE WITH IT.** His count is 173. The page goes out unsigned on the Monday morning and a copy goes to four bodies of households.

7. **390 (day 603, Sunday, the third of the ninth, the first line) - *He Disqualifies Himself*.** The boundary ditch and the two culverts, and the man of about thirty-one of Silling does not come down the road on a Sunday in eleven years. Launder **811**, a fall; the window at a hundred and twenty, sixty-five and fifty-five. Aggregate 151, 150 of 152. **The pair at 537 and 584 read aloud, forty-seven of seventy-seven.** Iona Vey is in the room at her own cost, unsent for, and asks for nothing and offers nothing. **HE GIVES THE REASON FIRST AT ONE HUNDRED AND SEVENTY-FOUR AND DISQUALIFIES HIMSELF OUT LOUD, THE REASON BEING A FACT ABOUT THE GROUND AND ABOUT A PAGE WITH A HOLE IN IT AND NOT ABOUT WHAT HE IS LIKE: THERE IS NO DATE IN THIS HOLDING'S BOOK AGAINST THE SECOND READING AND A MAN WHO HAS LOST A DAY CANNOT BE THE CHECK ON THE DAY, SO THE ASSESSMENT THAT CAME UP ON SATURDAY IS RIGHT AND HE IS NOT GOING TO BE THE SECOND THING THAT OFFICE IS RIGHT ABOUT.** **Nobody said sorry, nobody softened it, nobody asked whether it was right, and it is not a crisis and not a confession and nobody thanked anybody.** She writes that the reading stands and that he is not to be put forward as a check on it and the reason, and does not write that he thinks the office is wrong, because he has not said that, and does not write that he is sorry, for the same reason. He does not go up the road and does not go into the wood. The page goes out without a name on it and nobody in this holding is going to be that name.

8. **391 (day 604, Monday, the fourth of the ninth, the second line, and a return) - *Three Hundred And Twenty-Seven*.** The two gates and six feet of wall, the four of them still on it at the eighth hour. Launder **820**, a rise; the window at a hundred and twenty-one, sixty-six and fifty-five. Aggregate 152, 151 of 153. **The pair is not read aloud because the four on the wall went past the seventh hour and the man of about fifty had a return to set up at the node, and this page carries no figure for the run**; the pair stands at 538 and 585. **THE THIRTY-FIFTH NINTH-DAY RETURN GOES IN ON THE STEELYARD AND READS THREE HUNDRED AND TWENTY-SEVEN HUNDREDWEIGHT OUT LOUD AND READS IT BACK, THE TWENTY-FIFTH NAME-PAIR IN ELEVEN YEARS AND ELEVEN ABOVE THE THIRTY-FOURTH, RECONCILED TWICE OUT OF TWO HUNDRED AND SEVENTY-NINE PLUS FORTY-EIGHT AND TWO HUNDRED AND THIRTY-ONE PLUS NINETY-SIX, THE TWO HALVES NOT ADDED, AND THE PAGE SAYS ALOUD THAT THIS HOLDING IS USING THAT DERIVATION AND IS NOT REFUSING IT.** His count is 110, and the reason is that a figure which can only be arrived at one way is a figure somebody chose the way of, and he will not say which of the two he believes, because there is no believing to do and a sum is not a reason. **A name went into BY and a name into WITNESSED BY, one at a time, in the order the four came up. THE SECOND RULE WAS LEFT BLANK FOR THE NINETEENTH TIME IN ELEVEN YEARS AND THE COUNT OF BLANKS GOES EIGHTEEN TO NINETEEN, AND A COUNT OF BLANKS IS NOT THE COUNT OF A MAN.**

9. **392 (day 605, Tuesday, the fifth of the ninth, the third line) - *A Line That Is Not An Answer*.** The last morning of the forty-nine. The two places, the second of them empty four mornings running. Launder **815**, a fall; the window at a hundred and twenty-two, **sixty-six rises and fifty-six falls, and the two of them add**, and the count of the series is the hundred and fifty-fifth figure. Aggregate 153, 152 of 154. **The pair at 539 and 586 read aloud, forty-eight of seventy-nine, for the last time this year.** **THE MAN OF ABOUT FIFTY RULES A LINE IN THE SESSION BOOK AND ENTERS AGAINST IT THAT THE STANDING OF THE BRIDGE IS NOT IN THAT BOOK, AND WRITES NOTHING UNDER IT AND NOTHING ABOVE IT AND DOES NOT READ IT BACK, AND THAT IS THE ONLY PLACE IN THE WHOLE VOLUME THAT THE BRIDGE IS APPROACHED, AND IT SAYS WHERE A THING IS NOT AND NOT WHETHER THE THING IS.** Nobody said a word about it and about four people had been waiting four years for somebody to write down something about that bridge. **The rota stands at seventy-seven in force, twenty-nine taken and forty-eight not. The offer is on the low board, face up, not filled, refused on the nineteenth of a month now two back, not withdrawn, not taken up, no date and no line for a name. The register form is on the middle table at forty-nine days, not filled and not refused. The form with four lines is in a drawer four miles west with one hundred and eighty-four hundredweight on its first line and three empty lines under it. The corridor is named and open and neither closed nor opened. The ring is bare in its eleventh year with no dimension on any page. Six answers stand on who speaks for the eleven acres and none is an answer. The six not knowns are six and the not-known column took nothing for a bridge, a schedule, a man of about seventy or a sentence somebody else wrote.** The page ends with the day sheet going into the stack last, the drawer shut, and the figure for tomorrow going into the same book in the same hand and not being this one, **and the last line is not an answer.**

**BATCH 0003 — CHAPTERS 413 TO 422, DAYS 626 TO 635, MOVEMENT 3, *The Seizure*, 28,769 WORDS ACROSS TEN CHAPTERS.**

**Ch 413 (day 626, Tuesday, the twenty-sixth, the fourth line, 54 fields waited)** — *The Fourteenth Question*. The fourth line comes round at the second hour and is not worked, **the rota rises to eighty-three mornings in force with twenty-nine taken and fifty-four not, and BOTH COUNTS OF THE ROTATION ARE PRINTED, being thirty-one and eighteen.** About nine people in the one room with the door shut, and **the Assembly's motion goes to the first council and to the second by the ordinary post and by two riders, with the fourth clause sent separately so that the open offer and the seven hundred and four sacks are read in the same room by the same mouth.** **THE READER OF THIS BODY ASKS SOREN RILL ONE QUESTION AFTER THE ROOM IS FULL, being whether anybody is going to ask the four people of the Assembly whether they are the people who do that work, AND THE COUNT OF QUESTIONS HE HAS ASKED HIM GOES THIRTEEN TO FOURTEEN ON THAT PAGE AND NOWHERE ELSE.** The answer is no, and the reason given for it is that a question of that shape is a request and a request can be refused. **Marek, one hundred and ninety-four. The man of about fifty, one hundred and twenty-one.** The third launder is 864, a rise.

**Ch 414 (day 627, Wednesday, the twenty-seventh, the first line)** — *A Question In A County's Hand*. The first line is worked and **the read-aloud run is read at about the seventh hour at fifty-nine of a hundred and one, and the frame on the boards is said once.** The first council's letter asks in its second clause whether the taking of the heartroot has any effect on the drain that serves the west end and in which direction, and records that it is not asking whether the Assembly has a right. **Marek says he can answer it in about four minutes standing at the cut, gives the reason first, and does not write it out, because the question is a county's and the answer would become this building's and there is no column anywhere here that says what his name is answerable for. THE CLERK OF THIS HOLDING SAYS IT IN HIS OWN MOUTH, being that it is a county's question, that the answer if there is one is a county's, that it goes on the long table and not in a book, and that the fact that the engineer said he could answer it is entered and the answer is not.** No carrier is sent. **Marek, one hundred and ninety-five. The man of about fifty, one hundred and twenty-two.** The third launder is 859, a fall.

**Ch 415 (day 628, Thursday, the twenty-eighth, the second line, and a walk)** — *Four Miles And A Half, And A Chair With Nine In It*. **THE READER OF THIS BODY WALKS THE FOUR AND A HALF MILES TO THORNWILD AND BACK IN ONE DAY, ON FOOT, AND IT IS THE FIRST TIME THAT WALK HAS BEEN MADE BY ANY PERSON IN THIS HOLDING, AND THE COUNT OF THAT IS ONE, AND IT IS HIS, AND NOBODY THANKED HIM FOR IT.** He asks the Assembly for the heartroot back in about nine people with the door shut. **THE ASSEMBLY REFUSES, FOUR PEOPLE ANSWER HIM, EVERY ONE OF THEM GIVES THE REASON BEFORE THE THING, AND EVERY ONE OF THOSE REASONS IS A REASON HE HAS GIVEN OUT LOUD IN A ROOM IN FOUR YEARS; THE STRONGEST IS THAT A SETTLEMENT HARMED ONCE BY A CONNECTION IS ENTITLED TO BE ASKED, AND HAS BEEN ASKED, AND WAS GIVEN AN INSTRUMENT AND NOT AN ANSWER.** He is right and they are right and **the page says that being right is not a thing a man gets for free.** He puts his own name at the head of a page of his own with four lines of what he said and four of what was said back, the clerk reads all eight and improves none, **he is not thanked and is not forgiven and asked for neither, and nobody met him on the road.** **Tova Reed, thirty-seven, says she will give a figure for what a season of disconnection costs in seed without having got it, and says once that it does not get harder because of her left ear, and that anybody waiting nine days for a reason to take the seed work off her has not got one.** **Marek, one hundred and ninety-six.** The third launder is 868, a rise.

**Ch 416 (day 629, Friday, the twenty-ninth, the third line)** — *What A Decision Does Not Open*. **THE READ-ALOUD RUN IS READ AT SIXTY OF A HUNDRED AND THREE.** The second council's fourth clause records that the ground of the node it seized is shared on a line in the schedule with a county that was not asked before the resolution was carried and has not been asked since, and that the council will not send the trace to that county until the node is held. **EVERY WORD OF THAT LETTER IS CORRECT AND NOTHING IN IT IS A LIE, AN OBSTRUCTION, A DELAY OR A SOFTENING, and the man of about fifty says so in his own mouth and is asked twice for a sentence against the council and cannot supply one.** **THE CUT AT THE KERB STAYS OPEN, NOTHING HAS GONE INTO THE TWO-FOOT GAP THIS SEASON, THE VALVE IS NOT OPENED, THE KEY IS IN HER HAND AND IS NOT USED, AND THE DECISION OF THE ELEVENTH OF A MONTH FIVE MONTHS BACK IS NOT REOPENED BY ANYTHING IN THIS BUILDING.** **Marek, one hundred and ninety-seven, says the honest sentence is that a council is not going to be stopped before Saturday by anybody, and that he could have named that on Tuesday and was in a room with the door shut asking a different question.** The third launder is 863, a fall.

**Ch 417 (day 630, Saturday, the thirtieth, the fourth line, 55 fields waited, and the seizure)** — *The Assembly Takes The Node*. The fourth line comes round and is not worked and **the rota rises to eighty-four in force, twenty-nine taken and fifty-five not, and BOTH COUNTS OF THE ROTATION ARE PRINTED, being thirty-two and nineteen.** **THE SEVENTH COLUMN OF THE WELL HOUSE DOOR IS READ AT THE SEVENTH HOUR AND STANDS AT FIFTY-FIVE, AND FROM THIS MORNING IT DOES NOT GO BACK, AND IT IS READ AGAIN TOMORROW AND ON NO OTHER MORNING.** Four stakes go into the open ground on the north side of the node, with waxed covers and nothing written on them, and the woman at the middle of the Assembly reads out what they are for: that the reading of that ground is theirs and the answering of it is theirs. **It took about eleven minutes and there was no fight in it. THE BUILDING AT THE NODE WITH A BARROW IN IT IS NOT A YARD, THE SLOPE WITH ABOUT NINE PEOPLE ON IT IS NOT A YARD, THE COUNT OF THINGS SAID OUT LOUD IN A YARD IN THIS HOLDING AND GOT WRONG IS FIVE AND IT IS FIVE, AND THE CHAPTER SAYS SO TWICE.** The man of about fifty says he has run out of sentences that are against anybody. **Marek, one hundred and ninety-eight, says the honest sentence is that the Assembly is correct and is neither a right nor a wrong, and that nobody in this building has a way of knowing what a ground does when a body holds a thing that was never a valve, and that the six not knowns are six and he will not make a seventh out of an afternoon.** At the sixth hour the woman at the middle of the Assembly asks him what the dial reads when a body is not standing at it, and he tells her for about four minutes, and she thanks him for it in front of the other three, and he has not yet worked out what being thanked by somebody he lost an argument to on Thursday is going to be in about four years. The third launder is 872, a rise.

**Ch 418 (day 631, Sunday, the first of the tenth, and four clocks)** — *Four Things On One Morning*. **THE MONTH TURNS AND THE READ-ALOUD RUN IS READ AT SIXTY-ONE OF A HUNDRED AND FIVE, AND THE FRAME ON THE BOARDS AND THE RUN IS OF A MONTH FOUR MONTHS BACK FROM TODAY, AND THE CHANGE IS SAID HERE ONCE AND NOT TWICE.** **FOUR THINGS FELL ON THIS MORNING.** The man of about seventy was fetched at about the fourth hour, **being the twenty-fourth time, at thirty mornings' interval, he was in the one room from the fifth hour to the ninth, NOBODY ASKED HIM A SINGLE QUESTION, and the count of questions this holding has asked him is nil and is nil.** **THE COMPOST LINE FELL, THE WORD BEFORE THE FIGURE BEING PAID, THE FIGURE BEING ONE HUNDRED POUNDS, AND THE RUN TWENTY-ONE NOT DISCHARGED IN TWENTY-ONE, AND IT IS NOT A MEASUREMENT OF THE GROUND.** **THE SEVENTH COLUMN WAS READ AT THE SEVENTH HOUR AND STANDS AT FIFTY-SIX, AFTER FIFTY-FIVE YESTERDAY, AND THOSE TWO MORNINGS ARE THE SIXTH TIME IN FOUR YEARS IT HAS BEEN READ ON TWO DAYS RUNNING, AND THE COLUMN DOES NOT GO BACK.** **THE THIRTY-EIGHTH NINTH-DAY RETURN COMES OFF THE STEELYARD AT THREE HUNDRED AND SIXTY HUNDREDWEIGHT, THE TWENTY-EIGHTH PAIR OF NAMES IN ELEVEN YEARS, ELEVEN ABOVE THE THIRTY-SEVENTH, RECONCILED TWICE OUT OF THREE HUNDRED AND SIX PLUS FIFTY-FOUR AND TWO HUNDRED AND FIFTY-ONE PLUS A HUNDRED AND NINE, THE TWO HALVES NOT ADDED, AND THE SECOND RULE ON THE BOARD IS LEFT BLANK FOR THE TWENTY-SECOND TIME IN ELEVEN YEARS.** **THE MAN WHO KEEPS THE USE LOG GIVES THE REASON FOR THE FIFTEEN A SECOND TIME, FOUR YEARS AND A DAY AFTER THE FIRST, BECAUSE A SEASON TURNED LAST NIGHT, AND THE COUNT OF LINES IS FIFTEEN AND THE COUNT OF TELLINGS IS TWO AND THE TWO ARE NOT ADDED, AND NOBODY THANKED HIM FOR SAYING IT AGAIN.** **The man of about fifty, one hundred and twenty-four. Tova Reed, thirty-eight. Marek, one hundred and ninety-nine, who says four things fell because of the shape of a calendar and not because anybody arranged it.** The third launder is 867, a fall.

**Ch 419 (day 632, Monday, the second, and the outbreak)** — *What The Ground Does*. The second line is worked and the water in the boundary ditch is coming up through the silt at about the pace a man can walk. The ground at the node began to go wrong in the night after the taking and this is the second of the two mornings. **THE CHAPTER SAYS THE FOUR THINGS IN THAT ORDER, being that it is a consequence of damaged and contradictory patterns, that it is not an army, that it is not a command, and that it is nobody's fault, and the reason is given first and the count of that is two hundred.** A willow at about four hundred yards off the node lost a year's growth on its north side in one night, and a second willow ninety yards off put a season of soft wood on its south side, and the two are not in the same field and nobody has put them in it. **THE ASSEMBLY'S OWN RECORD COMES UP THE FEN ROAD, IS CORRECT IN EVERY PARTICULAR AND LETS NOTHING OUT, AND SAYS IT HAS NO POWER TO COMPEL ANY PERSON TO ANSWER THE READING AT THAT NODE.** **THE RING OF BARE GROUND IS THE ONE PLACE ON THAT NODE NOBODY CAN READ, A STAKE WENT OUTSIDE IT AT ABOUT THE ELEVENTH HOUR AND NOBODY WENT IN, AND IT WAS NOT WALKED AND NOT MEASURED AND NOT CROSSED AND NOT PRICED AND NOT EXPLAINED, AND THE OUTBREAK DID NOT PUT A DIMENSION ON IT.** **THERE WERE MORE THAN FIVE BODIES ON THAT NODE AND FIVE IS THE NUMBER ON THE PAGE, A COUNT OF FIVE BEING A FACT ABOUT A ROTA, AND THIS WAS NOT A YARD.** Somebody asks the man of about fifty for the figures in the pulse; he does not read it a third time and does not name it, **and he gives the reason AFTER the thing, and the reason is a fact about a page and not about a person, and the count of that in the holding's history did not move because the reason was not given first.** The third launder is 876, a rise.

**Ch 420 (day 633, Tuesday, the third)** — *No Command Over Consent*. The third line is worked and the run is read at **sixty-two of a hundred and seven**. **HE HOLDS THE PATTERN AT THE NODE FROM ABOUT THE TENTH HOUR AND THE FOUR PEOPLE OF THE ASSEMBLY WORK A STRIP ABOUT FOUR YARDS WIDE ON THE NORTH SIDE, AND HE ASKS ONE OF THEM TO MOVE AND ASKS THE SECOND ONE IN A DIFFERENT WAY WITH THE REASON GIVEN FIRST, AND NEITHER OF THEM MOVES, AND HE THEN SAYS OUT LOUD ONCE, IN ABOUT NINE PEOPLE, AT THE NODE, THAT THERE IS NO COMMAND OVER CONSENT AND THAT IT IS THE WHOLE OF WHAT HE HAS.** The Assembly's four stop about six yards short of the edge of the ring of bare ground because it is bare, **and have not been told that there is a thing on that node which cannot be read at all, and nobody in this holding is going to be in a position to stop them finding it out in about a week.** At the fourth hour a woman comes up the road and says there is somebody in the low ground between the two low points and asks for a cart and a hand. **NOBODY IN THIS BUILDING ASKS HER WHO IT IS AND THE TWO MEN WHO WENT DID NOT SAY WHAT THEY FOUND. THE PAGE NAMES NO PERSON WHO DID IT, BECAUSE NO PERSON DID IT, AND NAMES NO PERSON WHO COULD HAVE STOPPED IT, AND SAYS THAT THE READER OF THIS BODY IS ONE OF ABOUT NINE WHO COULD HAVE BEEN IN THAT LOW GROUND AT THE SIXTH HOUR AND WAS IN A ROOM AT THE FOURTH HOUR ASKING A BODY OF PEOPLE TO MOVE OFF FOUR YARDS OF GROUND. THE HURT IS NOT GIVEN A NUMBER AND IS NOT THE PRICE OF ANYTHING, AND THE ARGUMENT ABOUT FOUR YARDS OF GROUND WENT ON AFTER THE CART CAME BACK UP THE ROAD.** **Marek, two hundred and one, says being right is not a thing a man gets for free and also not a thing a man can use. Tova Reed, thirty-nine, says she has nothing to say about the low ground and says it anyway, and that it does not get harder because of her left ear.** The third launder is 871, a fall.

**Ch 421 (day 634, Wednesday, the fourth, the fourth line, 56 fields waited)** — *The Other End Is Not His*. The fourth line comes round and is not worked and **the rota rises to eighty-five mornings in force with twenty-nine taken and fifty-six not, and BOTH COUNTS OF THE ROTATION ARE PRINTED, being thirty-three and twenty.** **HE WAS NOT ONE OF THE SIX ON THE BOUNDARY DITCH THIS MORNING FOR THE FIRST TIME IN FOUR YEARS.** **THE FAR END OF THE BRIDGE IS HELD BY TWO PEOPLE, HARLAN VETCH AND THE MAN OF ABOUT SEVENTY-ONE OF SILLING, AND NEITHER OF THEM IS THE READER OF THIS BODY, AND WHAT WAS GIVEN UP WAS EXCLUSIVE ACCESS, WHICH IS THE WHOLE OF THE DIFFERENCE, AND IT WAS GIVEN UP IN ABOUT ELEVEN SECONDS AND NOBODY THANKED HIM FOR IT.** **A COUNT OF PATTERN-HOLDERS IS NOT A COUNT OF ENDS.** The clerk's entry says the standing of that bridge is in no book in this building **and that no person in this holding has an instrument that says whether it is on or off, and that the count of questions asked at that far end is nil before and nil after.** **HE ASKS THE WOMAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-EIGHT OF MARDEN ONE QUESTION, WHICH IS THE FIRST IN FOUR YEARS, BEING WHAT THE NUMBER SHE SAYS OUT LOAD IN ROOMS IS A NUMBER OF, AND THE COUNT OF QUESTIONS HE HAS ASKED HER GOES FROM NIL TO ONE, AND HER ANSWER IS THAT SHE HAS NEVER KNOWN, THAT HE WAS NOT GOING TO GET A UNIT OUT OF HER, AND THAT SHE IS NOT A SEVENTH OF THE SIX NOT KNOWNS.** A council asks this holding to enter a fifth account against the mark on his arm; **he refuses it with the reason first, and A REFUSAL IS NOT A FIFTH ACCOUNT, and the four accounts of that arm stand at four and are unreconciled. Marek, two hundred and two. The woman of about thirty-eight of Marden, nineteen. The man of about fifty, one hundred and twenty-five.** The third launder is 880, a rise.

**Ch 422 (day 635, Thursday, the fifth)** — *A Reading Is Not A Maintenance Act*. The first line is worked and the whole length of the low drain is done in four hours and a half, the quickest in this holding's history, and **the run is read at sixty-three of a hundred and nine.** A council's clerk asks that this holding read the dial at the node once a week, enter the reading, send it, and enter it **as a way of knowing what the ground wants**. **THE ANSWER ON THE PAGE IS THAT A READING IS NOT A MAINTENANCE ACT, THAT WHAT CAME OUT OF THE STANDING WILLOW ON THE TWENTY-NINTH OF A MONTH NOW TWO MONTHS BACK CAME OUT IN THE ORDER A WOOD KEEPS THINGS IN, THAT THE EIGHT PLACES THAT DID NOT COME OUT OF IT ARE NOT ON THE PAGE AND ARE NOT TO BE GUESSED AT, AND THAT THE COUNT OF LINES OUT OF THAT WOOD IS ELEVEN OF NINETEEN AND IS NOT TO BE GUESSED AT EITHER. Marek, two hundred and three.** The clerk asks whether a refusal goes back to the council or into the drawer, and it goes back, and nobody signed it. **THE COMFORT IN THAT WOOD IS NOT STANDING AND THE FATHER IS NOT ALIVE IN IT AND THE DAY DOES NOT COME BACK, AND NOTHING ANYBODY IN THAT ROOM IS ABOUT TO DO THIS MONTH BRINGS IT BACK.** **Tova Reed, forty, says the weekly number is the first number anybody in four counties has given her that she could put a figure next to, and that it is also the reason not to take it, and that it does not get harder because of her left ear.** The ground has gone back to about what it was on Monday, slowly, and nobody has said that is better. The third launder is 875, a fall.
